title: Bitcoin Could Rally Before Rate Cuts Begin, Binance Research Says
summary: Binance Research suggests slowing global monetary tightening could improve bitcoin’s outlook before central banks begin cutting interest rates, while growing use of tokenized equities in decentralized finance (DeFi) points to a new phase of blockchain adoption. Slowing Global Monetary Tightening Cou...
content:
Binance Research suggests slowing global monetary tightening could improve bitcoin’s outlook before central banks begin cutting interest rates, while growing use of tokenized equities in decentralized finance (DeFi) points to a new phase of blockchain adoption.

Key Takeaways

  • Binance Research found a -0.62 correlation between global tightening momentum and Bitcoin’s returns.
  • Binance’s Bstocks reached $1 billion in assets, with DeFi utilization exceeding the industry average.
  • Bitcoin’s 2027 outlook hinges on Fed policy, while tokenized stocks’ growth depends on sustained on-chain use.

Slowing Global Monetary Tightening Could Signal Bitcoin Recovery

Bitcoin (BTC) could benefit from an easing in the pace of global monetary tightening even as interest rates remain elevated, according to Binance Research. In its November 2026 Monthly Market Insights report, Binance’s research argues that the speed at which monetary tightening spreads across major economies may matter more for bitcoin than the actual level of interest rates.

According to the report, eight of the Group of 10 (G10) central banks raised interest rates over the preceding six months, while two kept rates unchanged. However, the pace at which monetary tightening spread across these economies has slowed since peaking in July.

The researchers used a monetary policy diffusion index that tracks whether central banks have raised, lowered, or maintained interest rates relative to six months earlier. Although the index remained elevated at 0.8, its six-month change had moderated from its July peak.

The report found a negative 0.62 correlation between changes in the index and bitcoin’s six-month returns since 2021, suggesting that BTC has historically performed better when the momentum of global tightening slows.

“For BTC, what matters is the speed at which tightening spreads, more than how widespread it is,” the report states.

Binance Research pointed to the previous monetary tightening cycle as evidence supporting its assessment. Bitcoin bottomed in November 2022, even though the diffusion index remained at its peak. The cryptocurrency’s six-month returns subsequently turned positive in February 2023, well before G10 central banks began easing monetary policy.

The researchers also cited the opposite trend in 2024, when widespread monetary easing coincided with bitcoin’s strongest six-month performance of that cycle, with returns exceeding 160% in March.

Fed Rate Decision Could Test Bitcoin’s Recovery Prospects

The report suggests a similar transition could be developing. Assuming no further monetary policy changes, the diffusion index would remain at 0.8 while its six-month momentum measure could decline to approximately 0.3 by January 2027.

Even additional rate increases by the remaining central banks would not necessarily reverse the slowdown, according to the researchers.

“If the historical relationship persists, the peak in tightening momentum marks a meaningful turn for BTC,” the report states.

However, the analysis does not establish that slowing tightening will necessarily trigger a sustained bitcoin recovery. Inflation, Treasury yields, and broader investor risk appetite remain important variables.

The Federal Reserve’s next policy decision could prove particularly consequential. At the time of the report, futures markets assigned an approximately 80% to 85% probability to a quarter-point rate increase in December, while the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield hovered around 5%.

A hawkish surprise could therefore prolong pressure on cryptocurrencies, even if the broader global tightening cycle continues losing momentum.

Tokenized Stocks Gain Momentum as DeFi Utilization Rises

Beyond the monetary policy outlook, Binance Research identified tokenized equities as an increasingly important area of cryptocurrency adoption, with growing evidence that investors are using blockchain-based securities for more than trading.

The report highlighted Binance’s Bstocks, which reached $1 billion in assets under management in just 125 days, less than half the time it took rival issuer Ondo to achieve the same milestone.

Since its launch in June, Bstocks has accounted for more than 60% of the growth in the tokenized stock market during the period examined, according to the researchers.
However, Binance Research argued that the platform’s onchain utilization rate offers a more meaningful measure of adoption than its rapid asset growth.

As of Oct. 31, Bstocks had an onchain utilization rate of 18.54%, compared with an industry average of 13.91%. The metric measures the proportion of active assets under management deployed in DeFi applications, including lending protocols and liquidity pools.

The difference suggests that investors are increasingly putting tokenized equities to work rather than merely holding them as digital representations of traditional securities.

“The depth of utilization is even more significant than the speed of issuance,” the report states.

The researchers argued that sustained growth in DeFi utilization allows tokenized equities to support increased lending and liquidity without needing to issue more tokens or rely solely on rising asset values. Moreover, this shift moves the focus of tokenization beyond initial issuance, settlement speed, and access toward maximizing the productive use of existing capital.

Binance Research identified growing demand for around-the-clock trading as a key driver of tokenized equity adoption, with 56% of Bstocks’ trading volume occurring outside regular U.S. market hours. Investors in emerging and frontier markets accounted for approximately 70% of trading activity, highlighting tokenization’s potential to expand access to global equities.

The report emphasized that sustained onchain utilization, rather than issuance growth alone, will determine the sector’s long-term success.

title: Can crypto trust firms compete with banks in US derivatives settlements?
summary: Crypto custodians are moving into a market handling billions in daily settlements, but regulatory relief and a shift in congressional control leave questions over their long-term role.
content:
Crypto companies are moving deeper into financial services traditionally dominated by banks, seeking a role in US derivatives settlements, where billions of dollars change hands daily.

The push comes as regulators expand the services trust companies can provide, even as traditional banking groups challenge parts of the regulatory framework governing crypto firms’ expansion into banklike activities.

A Nov. 5 decision by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) illustrates the shift, allowing derivatives clearinghouses to use trust companies for daily settlements with clearing members, a function previously restricted to banks under the agency’s regulations.

The relief could create new business opportunities for regulated crypto custodians, but its revocable nature and changes in the US political landscape raise questions about the durability of the regulatory opening.

Crypto firms eye billions in daily derivatives settlements

The scale of the derivatives settlement business offers some perspective on the opportunity.

CME Group, one of the world’s largest derivatives market operators, transferred an average of $8.7 billion per business day through its clearing systems during the first half of 2026, up from $6.7 billion a day in 2025, according to regulatory filings.

Those figures represent funds transferred between clearing firms to settle gains and losses, rather than fees earned by settlement banks. They nevertheless illustrate the scale of financial flows supported by the infrastructure that trust companies could increasingly help provide.

The CFTC’s Division of Clearing and Risk issued no-action relief on Nov. 5 following an Oct. 29 request from derivatives clearinghouse Nodal Clear, allowing clearinghouses to use trust companies for daily settlements if they meet the same evaluation and monitoring requirements applied to traditional settlement banks.

The decision addresses an inconsistency between federal commodities law, which permits customer funds to be held at banks or trust companies, and CFTC Regulation 39.14, which defines settlement banks only as banks.

Nodal Clear partnered with Coinbase in 2025 to integrate USDC into US futures trading. Coinbase Custody Trust was already expected to provide daily settlement services under the arrangement, Cointelegraph has learned.

Related: CFTC expands regulatory relief for passive trading software providers

Other crypto firms have also expanded their institutional financial services. On Nov. 4, BitGo launched its Global Markets division, combining derivatives trading, financing, collateral management and settlement capabilities.

Coinbase’s national trust bank charter also took effect on Nov. 6, allowing Coinbase National Trust Company, a separate entity from Coinbase Custody Trust, to provide federally supervised digital asset custody services.

Several major crypto firms have also secured US national trust bank approvals over the past months, including Circle, Ripple, Crypto.com and Stripe-owned Bridge. The charters, granted by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), reflect the industry’s expansion into federally regulated financial services.

Traditional banks contest crypto firms’ expanding role

The expansion of specialized trust companies has prompted objections from traditional banking groups.

In October, the Independent Community Bankers of America sued the OCC, arguing that its national trust bank charter rules could allow crypto firms to conduct certain banklike activities without meeting all the requirements imposed on conventional banks.

The lawsuit reflects a broader disagreement over how specialized financial institutions should be regulated as they expand into services also provided by banks.

Cody Carbone, CEO of The Digital Chamber, told Cointelegraph that the CFTC’s relief does not put trust companies in a better or worse position than traditional banks.

Trust companies and banks already compete for services permitted under their respective charters, Carbone said, adding that the decision gives clearinghouses more options without preventing banks from retaining their business. “A trust company charter is not a regulatory shortcut,” he said. 

Revocable relief faces a changing regulatory landscape

Despite the potential opportunities, the CFTC’s decision leaves questions about how securely trust companies can establish a long-term role in derivatives settlement.

The agency issued a no-action letter rather than formally amending its regulations. The letter states that CFTC staff will not recommend enforcement action against clearinghouses using trust companies for daily settlements if specified conditions are met.

Unlike a formal rule amendment, which generally requires a public notice-and-comment process, staff no-action relief does not change the underlying regulation and can be withdrawn.

“A change in Commission leadership could withdraw the CFTC Letter. More formal Commission action, such as amending the regulation, would be necessary to avoid this potential risk,” Jordan Yeagley, a shareholder at Buchanan Ingersoll & Rooney, told Cointelegraph.

The uncertainty comes at a politically significant moment for the agency. CFTC Chair Michael Selig remains the regulator’s sole commissioner, despite a statutory structure providing for five commissioners. Selig has led the agency since December 2025, leaving four seats vacant as the regulator expands its work on digital asset markets.

The political environment is also changing following the Nov. 3 US midterm elections, in which Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress.

The incoming Congress, which takes office in January, will have greater power to scrutinize the CFTC’s regulatory agenda. The Senate also has a role in confirming nominees to fill the agency’s vacant commissioner seats, while the House and Senate Agriculture Committees oversee the regulator.

Sen. Sherrod Brown, who won Ohio’s Senate race on Nov. 3 despite more than $60 million in opposition spending from crypto-backed political action committees, could take on a prominent role on the Senate Agriculture Committee.

title: LNbits Releases 1.7.0 Urgent Security Update After November 8 Attacks Drain Funds
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

LNbits Releases 1.7.0 Urgent Security Update After November 8 Attacks Drain Funds
LNbits released version 1.7.0 on November 10 as an urgent security update following active attacks that began November 8. Operators must upgrade before restarting servers as prior versions put funds a...
content:
LNbits, the open-source Lightning Network wallet and accounts platform, released version 1.7.0 on November 10 as an urgent security update and instructed all operators to upgrade before restarting their servers. The project’s official X account posted the announcement with a link to the GitHub release, calling it a “SECURITY UPDATE”.

The release follows a wave of attacks that began over the weekend. On November 8, LNbits posted on X that all users should stop their LNbits servers immediately after reporting active attacks, adding that security patches were being prepared and that it was “better to err on the side of caution.” 

The project also disabled instances on its hosted service. Multiple reports documented unauthorized account creation and fund withdrawals. 

Kevin Ravensberg, operator of the Telegram tipping service BitTipBot, publicly stated that attackers created new accounts on his instance and withdrew 2,285,545 satoshis (approximately 0.0229 BTC) between roughly 09:22 and 14:00 UTC on November 8.

According to the official upgrade guidance published alongside the release, versions prior to 1.7.0 are affected and “funds running on prior versions of LNbits are at risk of being stolen.” The project stated that 1.7.0 includes security fixes in response to the incident discovered on November 8 and that a full technical report on the exploit will follow. 

Operators are advised to set up a fresh server if compromise is suspected, because updating alone cannot remove access an attacker may already have gained. Additional recovery steps include rotating all user wallet keys as Super Admin, replacing funding-source credentials (API keys or macaroons), rotating other secrets stored in settings, and reviewing or re-creating connections for extensions such as NWC Provider, LNDHub, Bolt Cards, TPOS, Bleskomat, and FOSSA.

The GitHub release notes describe extensive security hardening across authentication, extension management, and payment handling, plus dependency updates. New features shipping with the version include on-chain wallet support, BOLT12 offer payments, TOTP two-factor authentication, NIP-17 support, a job scheduler, automatic extension updates, and hold invoice support for the LNbits funding source. The project notes that LNbits functions as a hot wallet and that operators should keep only operational balances online, regularly review activity, and move excess funds to offline keys.

LNbits was founded as a free and open-source project in 2019 by Ben Arc and later incorporated a commercial entity to support development. It provides multi-user accounts and a large suite of extensions on top of any Lightning funding source (including LND and Core Lightning). Bitcoin Magazine profiled the project in September 2024, describing it as “the WordPress for your Bitcoin Lightning node” noting its widepsread use by individuals, businesses, and node operators seeking accessible Lightning tooling. The software is widely deployed both self-hosted and via managed instances.

As of the v1.7.0 announcement, the project has not published an aggregate total of funds lost across all affected instances. Operators who have not yet upgraded are directed to the official guidance before bringing servers back online.

title: Across Protocol warns users to avoid app amid reports of drained wallets
summary: The protocol is investigating a potential security incident affecting its domain, while several users have reported losing funds after interacting with the platform.
content:
Crosschain bridging protocol Across, which allows users to transfer digital assets between Ethereum and other blockchain networks, warned users Tuesday not to access its app or connect their wallets while it investigates a potential security incident.

In a Tuesday X post, Across advised users against signing transactions or approvals until further notice, without specifying the nature of the incident or whether its website had been compromised.

Source: Across Protocol

On X, one user claimed to have lost $9,000 in USDC, while another reported losing 7,053 USDT0 across seven transactions on the Plasma blockchain.

A third user said their wallet was drained after using the bridge several times, alleging that the website had been compromised. Across asked the users for transaction details to investigate their reports.

Cointelegraph has not independently verified the reports. Across Protocol did not immediately respond to Cointelegraph’s request for more details.

Across Protocol responds to user reporting $9,000 USDC loss. Source: X user bilm01

NEAR AI discloses separate security breach

In a separate security incident, NEAR AI disclosed Monday that attackers exploited a vulnerability in its AI infrastructure, exposing account details belonging to approximately 100 users and data from 18 AI agents.

According to a Nov. 9 incident report, attackers exploited a remote code execution vulnerability in SGLang, an open-source AI inference engine, to gain access to an internal server and other infrastructure. The compromised data included user names, email addresses, agent chat histories, settings and logs, while two customers had API keys exposed.

NEAR AI said attackers may also have observed requests processed on the compromised server, including those running in confidential mode. The company said it had patched the vulnerability, revoked exposed credentials and restored access to its cloud services.

title: Ava Labs exec says NYSE deal marks end of blockchain’s ‘general purpose era’
summary: Ava Labs’ John Nahas said the collaboration with the NYSE shows institutions moving past pilots toward purpose-built onchain market infrastructure.
content:
Traditional finance is moving past one-size-fits-all blockchains, according to John Nahas, chief business officer at Ava Labs, the company behind the Avalanche network.

Nahas told Cointelegraph that the planned NYSE-affiliated tokenized securities platform, which will use Avalanche technology for clearing and settlement, illustrates that financial institutions want more control over how their blockchains operate.

“Capital markets need reliable performance and predictable cost settlement, certainty and control over the network and its participants,” he said. “It’s really important for this chain to be purpose built for the needs of NYSE.”

Nahas argued that the crypto industry’s preference for general-purpose blockchains and its reluctance to adapt to the compliance rules financial institutions face have slowed adoption.

“Crypto always wants to put the crypto part front and center,” Nahas said. He sees a shift toward blockchains designed for specific use cases. “I look at this as the end of the general purpose era,” he said.

Related: Avalanche’s AVAX leads crypto gains following NYSE tokenization deal

Adjusting to institutional needs

The NYSE move, announced on Monday, comes as more companies object to third parties tokenizing their shares for trading on OKXICE, a separate venue proposed by crypto exchange OKX and NYSE parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). OKXICE listed 67 companies that had objected as of Nov. 5, including Apple, Amazon, Meta and Tesla.

Nahas put the pushback down partly to a lack of understanding among incumbents, who he said see crypto as a speculative “wild west.” He said a “wholesale change” to market infrastructure built around institutions’ needs would make the potential efficiency gains clearer and expected objecting companies would “come around.”

Dennis Lee, the NYSE’s head of digital issuance, said the exchange will be “picking the right technology for each job,” as its develops the platform.

Although the NYSE-affiliated platform will support equities issued on a variety of blockchains, the settlement ledger had to allow the exchange to “control who can take part and keep costs predictable,” both elements Lee said Avalanche met. On public blockchains, such as Ethereum, institutions can restrict access to their own applications, while the underlying networks remain open. Congestion can also drive up transaction fees.

The NYSE spent a year testing Avalanche, giving Ava Labs time to tailor its approach to the exchange’s needs, Nahas said.

“The problem is general purpose chains don’t want to or most of the time cannot adapt to the existing frameworks,” he said.

Resilience to changing landscape

Nahas said the ability to adapt matters most when regulations are still taking shape. “Nobody wants to be on the wrong side of a line that didn’t exist the day before,” he said. In his view, building around the rules financial institutions already follow can help projects move forward while regulators clarify how those rules apply to crypto.

Asked what the “blue wave” in the House and Senate could mean for the US crypto industry, Nahas said he remained optimistic. “The landscape has changed, but the underlying fact is that this train has left the station,” he said. “You see that today in a big way.”

title: MARA Sells 13,597 Bitcoin for $1.1B as Its AI Pivot Reshapes Treasury Strategy
summary: MARA disclosed $1.1 billion of post-quarter Bitcoin sales and repayment of $750 million in BTC-backed borrowing. The miner is increasingly monetizing…
content:
MARA has put a sizeable number on the changing economics of Bitcoin mining. In its third-quarter shareholder letter, the company said it sold 13,597 BTC after September 30 for approximately $1.1 billion, at an average selling price of about $81,039. It used $750 million of the proceeds to repay Bitcoin-collateralized loans, releasing 17,477 BTC that had been pledged as security.

TL;DR: MARA disclosed $1.1 billion of post-quarter Bitcoin sales and repayment of $750 million in BTC-backed borrowing. The miner is increasingly monetizing its coin reserves to support AI infrastructure and other capital priorities. This marks a meaningful departure from its earlier strategy of holding mined Bitcoin.

The balance-sheet logic behind the sale

At the end of September, MARA reported 34,012 BTC in total holdings, including a sizeable portion lent out or pledged as collateral. The newly disclosed disposals followed quarter-end, so that September balance should not be presented as the company’s current holding without adjustment. MARA said the repayments reduced the proportion of Bitcoin lent or pledged to less than 5% of its remaining holdings, versus roughly 57% at the earlier reporting date.

Management describes the move as a way to gain financial flexibility while still using Bitcoin strategically. Borrowing against the coins had helped finance the proposed acquisition of the Long Ridge natural-gas power business. The subsequent sale allowed MARA to clear the borrowing before the transaction closed, instead of leaving its financing exposed to future collateral calls if Bitcoin weakened.

That is a trade-off, not a free improvement. Selling reserve assets reduces direct exposure to any subsequent Bitcoin recovery. Keeping more BTC would preserve that upside but could require accepting additional liquidity and borrowing risk. The appropriate decision depends on the company’s priorities and its ability to earn a return on the infrastructure being funded.

Mining and AI now compete for the same capital

MARA’s third-quarter revenue fell about 35% from a year earlier to $164.2 million. Its mining operations still produce coins, but the company is now emphasizing power assets and potential data-center customers alongside hashrate. Long Ridge includes generating capacity and land that could support a data-center campus. Development plans are not the same as signed, revenue-producing leases.

The move also fits a wider sector pattern. NewsBTC recently reported how Riot sold more than 20,000 BTC while pursuing AI-related data-center agreements. The contrast with Strive’s rapid Bitcoin accumulation is useful: public companies can use the same underlying asset in radically different corporate strategies.

What investors should read past the headline

MARA also disclosed authorization for up to $500 million in share repurchases, while its reported quarterly profit included substantial accounting effects linked to digital assets. Those items should not be mistaken for recurring mining cash flow. Nor does an authorization guarantee that every dollar of the program will be spent.

The follow-up questions are whether Long Ridge closes, whether planned data-center leases are signed, how much Bitcoin remains unrestricted, and whether new AI revenue eventually justifies the capital committed. The BTC sale is confirmed. The return on the assets it may finance is still an execution story.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Wall Street Banks Commit $270M to Stablecoin Challenger Project Faro: Bloomberg
summary: A formidable coalition of 21 financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, and Bank of America, has committed approximately $270 million to a joint stablecoin venture known internally as Project Faro. According to “people familiar with the matter,” speaking with Bloomberg, the banking ...
content:
A formidable coalition of 21 financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, and Bank of America, has committed approximately $270 million to a joint stablecoin venture known internally as Project Faro. According to “people familiar with the matter,” speaking with Bloomberg, the banking consortium is targeting a commercial launch in 2027.

Key Takeaways

  • Project Faro’s $270 million commitment will finance five years of operations, separate from the reserves backing its stablecoins.
  • The venture unites 21 financial institutions across five continents, Bloomberg reports, with a U.S. dollar stablecoin planned first.
  • The consortium is recruiting a CEO as it prepares to challenge established stablecoin issuers in 2027.

Banking Giants Assemble $270 Million Stablecoin War Chest

According to Bloomberg, the consortium’s $270 million commitment will cover the first five years of operating expenses for a new U.S.-incorporated stablecoin issuer. The funding is distinct from the reserves supporting the digital currency, which participants expect to maintain on a 1:1 basis using eligible assets.

The initiative reportedly brings together some of traditional finance’s most influential institutions, including Goldman Sachs, Citi, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Fidelity Investments, Deutsche Bank, Santander, UBS, and Capital One. Other participants include PNC Financial Services, Scotiabank, TD Bank Group, Wisdomtree, BBVA, Commerzbank, Crédit Agricole, Lloyds Banking Group, Rabobank, MUFG Bank, Sirius International Holding, and Standard Bank.

The consortium’s origins stretch to October 2025, when 10 banks began exploring reserve-backed digital currencies operating on public blockchains. By Sept. 1, 2026, participation had purportedly expanded to 21 institutions, which announced plans to establish a dedicated company.

Project Faro remains an internal designation rather than an official corporate name. Bloomberg’s Anna Irrera and Arno Schuetze report that participants are searching for a CEO while preparing for a commercial launch during the first half of 2027.

Can Project Faro Challenge Tether and Circle?

The proposed issuer enters a stablecoin market valued at nearly $290 billion, where Tether’s USDT and Circle’s USDC collectively account for roughly 85% of outstanding supply.

Unlike cryptocurrency-native competitors, Project Faro’s stablecoin idea intends to capitalize on established banking relationships, international payment networks, and institutional distribution. Its initial dollar-pegged token would serve wholesale, institutional, and retail markets, with cross-border payments and digital asset settlement among the intended applications.

A euro-denominated stablecoin is expected to follow, potentially extending the venture into additional Group of Seven currencies. Regulatory compliance represents another central consideration. The consortium intends to operate within the U.S. GENIUS Act and Europe’s Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) framework, as applicable.

Signed into law July 18, 2025, the GENIUS Act establishes reserve, disclosure, and supervisory requirements for permitted payment stablecoin issuers, providing a clearer legal foundation for regulated dollar-backed tokens. The regulatory framework is expected to take effect in January 2027.

Nevertheless, considerable uncertainties remain. The consortium has not disclosed its preferred blockchain networks, reserve custody arrangements, redemption infrastructure, or final ownership structure. Its plans also remain subject to closing conditions. The stealth project comes at a time when the stablecoin supply and the tokenized U.S. treasury market have witnessed a downturn over the last month.

The $270 million commitment demonstrates considerable institutional ambition, but financial backing alone cannot guarantee adoption. Project Faro must still secure approvals, establish dependable infrastructure and persuade customers to embrace its token. Ultimately, the venture’s greatest test will be converting banking influence into genuine stablecoin demand.

title: Texas Rep. Files Bill Letting Cities Invest $10 Million in Bitcoin
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Texas Rep. Files Bill Letting Cities Invest $10 Million in Bitcoin
Rep. Ron Reynolds filed House Bill 815 on Monday, allowing each Texas city or county to put up to $10 million of public money into bitcoin starting Sept. 1, 2027.
This post Texas Rep. Files Bill Letting Cities Inves...
content:
A Texas lawmaker filed a bill Monday that would let each city and county in the state invest up to $10 million of public money in bitcoin or another cryptocurrency, without setting any rules for how those coins would be held.

House Bill 815, filed by Rep. Ron Reynolds, a Missouri City Democrat, on the first day of prefiling for the 90th Texas Legislature, carries the caption “Relating to the authority of a municipality or county to invest money in cryptocurrencies.” The introduced text, posted on the Texas Legislature’s site, is two sections long.

The bill would amend the Public Funds Investment Act, Chapter 2256 of the Texas Government Code, by adding a new Section 2256.0165, titled “Authorized Investments: Cryptocurrency.” Under that section, “a municipality or county may invest not more than $10 million of its money or money under its control in Bitcoin or another cryptocurrency.” The authority would take effect Sept. 1, 2027, if the bill becomes law.

The $10 million figure is a cap on each city or county, not a single statewide pool. School districts and other local governments covered by the investment act are left out.

What the bill does and does not say

The measure borrows its definitions of “Bitcoin” and “cryptocurrency” from Section 403.701 of the Government Code, the definitions written into law last year by Senate Bill 21, which created the Texas Strategic Bitcoin Reserve. Bitcoin is defined as a decentralized cryptocurrency created by a peer-to-peer network that operates independently of any central authority or bank. Cryptocurrency is defined more broadly as a virtual currency that uses cryptography to secure transactions recorded on a distributed ledger, such as a blockchain.

That means a city or county would not be limited to bitcoin. The bill also does not import the reserve law’s requirement that coins bought for the state fund have an average market capitalization of at least $500 billion over the most recent 24-month period, or its provisions on cold storage and qualified custodians.

The Public Funds Investment Act already requires local governments to adopt a written investment policy that emphasizes safety of principal and liquidity, and to invest with the care a prudent person would use in managing their own affairs. A city or county would still have to add cryptocurrency to that policy before buying any. The new section itself is silent on custody, on audits specific to digital assets, and on how a loss would be handled.

A narrower version of last year’s proposal

Reynolds filed a broader measure, House Bill 4258, on March 10, 2025, with Rep. Mihaela Plesa. That bill would have let the comptroller invest as much as $250 million of the Economic Stabilization Fund, the state’s rainy day fund, in bitcoin or another cryptocurrency, and it included the same $10 million cap for cities and counties. It was referred to the House Delivery of Government Efficiency Committee on April 1, 2025, and did not become law.

House Bill 815 drops the rainy day fund language and keeps only the local-government piece. The state’s own reserve was created separately through Senate Bill 21, which Gov. Greg Abbott signed in June 2025.

The Texas Comptroller’s office later bought $5 million of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust on Nov. 20, 2025, as a placeholder while it worked on direct custody, The Texas Tribune reported, with the office confirming the purchase. A second purchase brought the reserve’s IBIT exposure to about $10 million. In May, Acting Comptroller Kelly Hancock named an advisory committee and issued a request for proposals for a custodian, a step toward holding bitcoin directly.

What comes next

Prefiling for the 90th Texas Legislature opened Monday, and the regular session convenes Jan. 12, 2027. The bill has been filed but has not yet been referred to a committee, a step that typically waits until lawmakers convene. Even if it passes both chambers and is signed, cities and counties could not use the new authority until Sept. 1, 2027.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Ether ETFs Shed $184.6M in a Day as BlackRock Leads Redemptions
summary: US spot Ether ETFs lost $184.6 million on November 9. BlackRock's ETHA recorded $119.3 million in outflows, with additional withdrawals from several…
content:
The latest numbers from US spot Ether exchange-traded funds are another reminder that crypto’s institutional wrappers do not always move in sync with the networks beneath them. Farside Investors reports $184.6 million of net withdrawals on Monday, November 9. BlackRock’s ETHA accounted for $119.3 million, making it the largest identifiable contributor to the day’s negative reading.

TL;DR: US spot Ether ETFs lost $184.6 million on November 9. BlackRock’s ETHA recorded $119.3 million in outflows, with additional withdrawals from several other products. The latest session extends a run of weakness, but ETF flows alone cannot tell investors whether Ethereum’s network use or long-term adoption is improving.

The distribution of Monday’s redemptions

Monday’s fund table is more revealing than a single headline number. Besides ETHA, the negative entries included Grayscale’s ETH product at $25 million, BlackRock’s ETHB at $20.8 million, Fidelity’s FETH at $19.1 million and TETH at $2 million. Morgan Stanley’s MSSE reported a smaller $1.6 million positive flow. Netting these issuer-level movements produces Farside’s total of $184.6 million leaving the category.

It was the third consecutive negative session, after withdrawals of $99.9 million on November 5 and $93.3 million on November 6. Across those dates, approximately $377.8 million left the tracked funds on a net basis. NewsBTC’s earlier look at the November 5 outflow provides a useful baseline, while our October divergence report shows how quickly relative Bitcoin and Ether fund demand can change.

ETF investors are not the entire Ethereum economy

An ETF owns or obtains exposure to ETH for its shareholders. It does not capture every place ETH is held, used as collateral, staked or exchanged. The Ethereum network also supports stablecoin transfers, decentralized finance applications, tokenized securities and settlement activity. Those services can grow or contract independently of whether a US investment wrapper receives subscriptions on a particular day.

Equally, network activity is not automatically a bullish signal for ETH’s market price. Fees, token issuance, layer-two activity and competition for users influence how economic use may translate into demand for the asset. Sensible analysis keeps both sets of evidence in view rather than choosing whichever currently supports a favored market narrative.

A useful comparison with Bitcoin, and an important caveat

Bitcoin funds also recorded negative flows on November 9. That indicates this is not simply a one-day rotation from ETH into BTC within the US spot ETF category. Still, the products differ in investor base, structure, age and exposure, so the two daily totals should not be converted into a precise conclusion about relative institutional conviction.

One additional complication is reporting timing. Daily ETF tables are finalized after the US market closes and may be revised when an issuer reports late. Quoting an unfinished session as a completed result could create a false impression of reversal or acceleration. The figures here are dated specifically to November 9, and that time stamp should remain with the headline wherever the article is shared.

The next completed sessions will show whether ETHA’s withdrawals persist and whether other products begin drawing offsetting demand. Until then, Monday’s figures are strong evidence of weak investment-fund flows—not a definitive reading of the wider Ethereum economy or a forecast of the token’s next move.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Grayscale Pledges $1M to Zcash Ecosystem as ZEC Plunges Below $1,000
summary: Grayscale paired a $1 million Zcash ecosystem commitment with a new education platform and Wall Street Journal advertisements. The national campaign promoted its Zcash fund alongside grants supporting network development, policy advocacy, and financial privacy education.   Four Zcash Groups Receive ...
content:
Grayscale paired a $1 million Zcash ecosystem commitment with a new education platform and Wall Street Journal advertisements. The national campaign promoted its Zcash fund alongside grants supporting network development, policy advocacy, and financial privacy education.

Key Takeaways

  • Four Zcash groups were awarded a combined $400,000, with Grayscale planning a total $1 million in grants.
  • Grayscale plans to reinvest 100% of fund management fees for up to a year.
  • Campaign placements included a newspaper wrap and full-page ZCSH ad.

Four Zcash Groups Receive Initial Grant Awards

Grayscale launched Zcash Invest on Nov. 10 and committed $1 million to organizations and initiatives supporting the network. Its $1 million funding commitment included an initial $400,000 awarded through four equal grants. The recipients were the Zcash Foundation, Pretty Good Policy for Zcash, Shielded Labs, and Project Tachyon.

The foundation supports open-source development and financial privacy research, while Pretty Good Policy for Zcash is a nonprofit advocacy group educating policymakers. Shielded Labs, a Swiss-based organization, researches and develops Zcash network technology. Project Tachyon is a protocol initiative led by one of Zcash’s co-founders intended to help wallets update faster and process more private transactions.

Steve Vanourny, Grayscale’s head of index, stated:

“We believe Zcash will help define the next era of crypto.”

He linked financial privacy demand to growing blockchain activity and AI’s ability to analyze it. His comments also identified quantum computing as a future technological challenge.

National Campaign Reaches The Wall Street Journal

Zcash Invest targets investors and advisers through a website, social media presence, and educational content. The Zcash investor education platform also highlights the Zcash ETF, a fund holding ZEC whose shares trade under ticker ZCSH. Its launch accompanied the national campaign “Zcash: The Next Era of Crypto.”

Newspaper placements included a front-page wrap promoting Zcash and a full-page interior advertisement highlighting ZCSH in The Wall Street Journal. Zebra-striped artwork drew on imagery associated with the Zcash community. Planned distribution spans print, outdoor advertising, digital media, streaming, and social channels, alongside events and educational material.

Growing analytical capabilities underpin Grayscale’s financial privacy argument: AI could connect public blockchain activity with real-world identities. Zcash supports transparent transactions and shielded transfers, which conceal payment details. These private payments use cryptographic proofs to validate transactions without revealing sender and recipient addresses or amounts.

Fund Fees Back Development as ZEC Falls

Grayscale intends to reinvest 100% of the sponsor fees it receives from ZCSH for up to 12 months following the registration statement’s effectiveness. These management fees would support the fund and Zcash development, marketing, and education. Grayscale pays from its own funds after receiving the fees, and may modify or discontinue the voluntary undertaking.

ZCSH began trading on NYSE Arca on Aug. 25, following its 2017 private-placement launch and 2021 over-the-counter trading debut. Brokerage shares provide indirect ZEC exposure. Despite its ETF name, the product is not registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940, which governs conventional mutual funds and ETFs.

Shareholders gain exposure without buying or safeguarding tokens, avoiding the wallet-management requirements associated with holding cryptocurrency directly.

Security concerns prompted Zcash’s Ironwood network upgrade on July 28 after a vulnerability was discovered in Orchard, a system for holding and transferring ZEC privately. Ironwood introduced a replacement shielded pool and capped withdrawals from Orchard at verifiably deposited amounts, limiting movement of hypothetical counterfeit coins.

As of this writing, ZEC traded at $1,033 on Nov. 10, down about 12% over the last 24 hours. That’s up slightly from a low of $999.57 earlier Tuesday—the lowest price registered for the privacy coin since early September. Even so, at its current price, ZEC has more than doubled in value since the start of the year.

Who Can Claim It?

What are the requirements?

The BloFin mystery box reward tasks must be completed within 7 days, followed by another 7 days to claim the box under the linked terms. The larger deposit and trading volume challenge must be completed within 14 days.

Verdict on the BloFin Offer

The BloFin offer fits a futures trader who wants a simple no-KYC trading platform and can finish tasks quickly. It is kind of weak for a long-term holder because most of the reward has value only during futures activity. 

Also, make sure you use our referral code [cryptoninjas], as it rewards you with up to a $5,000 crypto sign-up bonus and 20% trading fee rebates.

9. KuCoin

KuCoin offers a sign-up bonus worth up to 10,800 USDT, spread across deposit tiers, plus an instant reward for finishing your first few sign-up actions. It is known as the “People’s Exchange” and lists over 1,500 digital assets across spot and futures markets. Honestly, KuCoin offers some of the best altcoin selection in the crypto world.

How to Get the KuCoin Sign-Up Bonus?

  1. Create an Account: The bonus requires you to create a new account with the KuCoin invitation code: “freebonus”.
  2. ID Verification: Complete KYC verification right after you sign up. This will give you a 50 USDT cash reward.
  3. Deposit: Make a deposit and place your first trade to instantly unlock another 100 USDT sign-up bonus.
  4. Reach trading Volume Milestones: Deposit 100 USDT with 1,000 USDT in trading volume for another 100 USDT, the entry deposit tier.

Who Can Claim It?

New KYC-approved KuCoin users from supported regions can claim the package. KuCoin requires identity verification for normal new account access and trading. 

Plus, U.S. users cannot open or use the global platform, and KuCoin also lists Singapore, mainland China, Hong Kong, Malaysia, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, France, the Netherlands, and parts of Canada among current restricted locations.

What are the requirements?

You must complete sign-up bonus tasks within 30 days of registration. This includes KYC, deposit, and reaching trading volume milestones. 

  • 100 USDT Bonus: Deposit 100 USDT and achieve 1,000 USDT trading volume
  • 400 USDT Bonus: Deposit 1,000 USDT and achieve 10,000 USDT trading volume
  • 800 USDT Bonus: Deposit 5,000 USDT and achieve 30,000 USDT trading volume
  • 1,500 USDT Bonus: Deposit 10,000 USDT and achieve 50,000 USDT trading volume
  • 8,000 USDT Bonus: Deposit 100,000 USDT and achieve 200,000 USDT trading volume

Verdict on the KuCoin Offer

The KuCoin offer is strong for altcoin, bot, and futures traders who already want to use several exchange products. The US exit is a serious limitation though, and it’s not a short-term thing given the multi-year settlement terms involved. But traders outside the US still get one of the more rewarding sign-up packages on this entire list.

10. Margex

Margex gives new users a $50 sign-up bonus and a separate first-deposit bonus that can be up to $10,000 in bonuses. But it keeps its crypto sign-up bonus refreshingly simple: a flat $50 credited the moment you register, no deposit required at all.

How to Get the Margex Sign-Up Bonus?

  1. Create an Account: You must enter referral code “YYY” when you sign up, then claim your bonus manually since it doesn’t apply automatically.
  2. Deposit Funds: Since KYC is optional, deposit $100 or more in any supported cryptocurrency to unlock a second first deposit bonus. You need to claim that second bonus within 7 days of registering, since it expires after that window closes.
  3. Trading Volume: You can also grab up to $10,000 in additional bonus depending on your trading volume.

Who Can Claim It?

Margex bonus can be claimed by all new users on the exchange. But remember, the platform is not available in the United States, Seychelles, Bermuda, Cuba, Iran, Syria, North Korea, Sudan, and other restricted areas. Sometimes, account verification may be required for security reasons, even though Margex does not always require standard KYC for basic crypto trading.

What are the requirements?

  • You genuinely just need to register an account to unlock the $50 sign-up bonus.
  • You must claim your bonus from the “Promo Code Storage”, since it doesn’t credit itself automatically.
  • Plus, deposit at least $100 within 7 days to claim the “First Deposit Bonus” as well.
  • You can treat your bonus funds as cashback, not free cash, since they cover up to 50% of trading fees and funding costs once trades close.

Verdict on the Margex Offer

The Margex offer has one of the easiest entry points because the $50 sign-up credit needs no large trading target. Mainly, its real value remains limited to fee and funding cost coverage. So, it works best for someone who already plans to use Margex leverage trading.

How We Verified These Welcome Bonus Offers?

We verified these welcome offers by checking the four criteria: offer value, trading volume requirement, expiration, and eligible regions.

  • Offer value: We separated the headline maximum from the amount a normal new user can reach. You see, a package worth 30,000 USDT may include a small sign-up reward, but a much larger futures tier for high-volume traders. We also checked whether the reward comes as withdrawable crypto, a fee rebate, a mystery box, a trading bonus, or a trial fund.
  • Trading Volume requirement: We compared the required net deposit with the spot or futures volume needed for each tier. Plus, we also checked common exclusions such as internal transfers, zero-fee trades, API activity, bot volume, and subaccounts.
  • Duration: We checked how long you have to finish a task, claim a completed reward, and use the claimed voucher. You see, every crypto exchange sign-up bonus has an expiry date, generally within 30 days of registration.
  • Eligible regions: We compared the campaign country rules with each exchange’s current restricted-location terms. A referral link may open in your browser even though your verified country cannot join the offer. We also treated U.S. versions of Binance and OKX as separate services because their global bonuses and products do not automatically carry over.

Are crypto sign-up bonuses worth it?

Yes, crypto sign-up bonuses are genuinely worth claiming in most cases, as long as you go in with realistic expectations about what you’ll actually receive. 

The instant, low-effort tiers, like Binance’s KYC voucher or even Margex’s flat $50, cost you basically nothing beyond a few minutes of setup. But again, the bigger headline numbers, like Bybit’s $30,020 or MEXC’s $10,000, require serious capital and trading volume that most casual users will never reach, so you should treat those as aspirational rather than expected.

You see, no-deposit bonus offers are rare, and a free crypto sign-up bonus with instant withdrawal usually comes with a lock, KYC step, or trading condition. The better way is to value a bonus at what you can personally use. Also, most of the bonus funds usually arrive as trading credit or vouchers rather than withdrawable cash. Hence, at least at first, read the terms before assuming you can cash out immediately.

Which crypto exchange sign-up bonus is the best for your trading type?

The best crypto sign-up bonus, or welcome reward, depends more on how you plan to use the exchange. According to the definition of crypto welcome bonus, the first-time account openers may benefit more from simple deposit or first-trade rewards, while buy-and-hold investors should look for those bonuses that never require heavy trading, and frequent traders often get more from fee discounts and similar exchange promotions.

Next, high-frequency and grid traders can usually get more value from trading-fee rebates, volume-based sign-up rewards, and futures bonuses because they trade more often.

First-Time Account Openers

First-time account openers should choose a bonus with very simple requirements and a low minimum deposit. You know, a reward for completing KYC, making your first deposit, or placing a few trades makes more sense than a large bonus that requires thousands of dollars in trading volume. Hence, you should mainly focus on how easy the reward is to unlock rather than its maximum advertised value.

Buy-and-Hold Investors

Buy-and-hold investors should look for deposit bonuses or rewards that require little trading. Basically, a $50 reward after depositing and buying crypto can be more useful than a $500 futures bonus that requires active trading. Plus, you should also avoid promotions that force you to generate high trading volume because frequent buying and selling does not match a long-term investment strategy.

High-Frequency and Grid Traders

High-frequency and grid traders can benefit most from bonuses linked to trading volume. Here, fee rebates, futures credits, trading vouchers, and volume-based rewards become more valuable because you naturally place many trades. Hence, a bonus with a higher trading requirement may therefore make sense for you, provided the normal trading fees and conditions remain competitive.

Are free crypto sign-up bonuses available for every exchange?

No, free crypto sign-up bonuses are not available on every exchange. Not every platform uses the same signup structure, and some reserve free bitcoin or similar promotions for app-based campaigns or limited regions. Basically, each platform decides its own promotion rules, and some exchanges do not offer any reward just for creating an account.

Even exchanges that advertise a welcome bonus usually ask you to complete certain steps first. So, you may need to verify your identity, deposit a minimum amount, make your first trade, or reach a required trading volume. The reward can also vary by country, campaign period, and referral link.

Can I withdraw my free crypto bonuses immediately?

No, you cannot withdraw a free crypto bonus immediately, as most exchanges place conditions on the reward because the bonus is meant to encourage real trading activity, not simply give away withdrawable cash.

You should also check the exchange app terms carefully, since bonuses can vary by region and some platforms use promotions to grow their user base.

You may need to deposit funds, complete KYC, make a certain number of trades, or reach a required trading volume before the bonus even becomes eligible for withdrawal. Plus, some rewards cannot be withdrawn at all. So, for example, futures bonuses and trading credits may only cover trading losses or fees, while you can withdraw the profits earned from them under certain rules.

Of course, this works differently from exchange to exchange. Hence, you should always check the withdrawal terms first, especially the minimum trading requirement, expiry date, and whether the bonus itself or only the profits can be withdrawn.

title: XRP Ledger Targets Quantum-Resistant Upgrade by 2028—The Risks and Costs
summary: The XRP Ledger Foundation has outlined a proposed upgrade to protect XRP accounts and network validators against future quantum computing attacks, detailing the technical requirements, costs, and potential challenges of adopting quantum-resistant cryptography. XRP’s Path to Post-Quantum Cryptography...
content:
The XRP Ledger Foundation has outlined a proposed upgrade to protect XRP accounts and network validators against future quantum computing attacks, detailing the technical requirements, costs, and potential challenges of adopting quantum-resistant cryptography.

Key Takeaways

  • XRP Ledger is targeting quantum readiness by 2028, with new roadmap research outlining plans to implement ML-DSA-44 post-quantum signatures for accounts, validators, and validator list publishers.
  • The upgrade presents significant technical challenges, including a 213% increase in transaction size, an estimated 1,040 development and review hours, and $215,000 to 255,000 in additional expenses.
  • Other major blockchains are also preparing for quantum threats, including Ethereum, Solana, Bitcoin, and Starknet, as developers explore new cryptographic standards and network upgrades to protect against future quantum attacks.

XRP’s Path to Post-Quantum Cryptography

The research, published as part of the XRP Ledger Foundation’s 2027 protocol roadmap, examines introducing ML-DSA-44, a standardized post-quantum digital signature algorithm, across the blockchain’s accounts, validators, and validator list publishers.

The proposed change would allow users and network operators to replace existing cryptographic keys with alternatives designed to withstand attacks from sufficiently powerful quantum computers.

The research builds on Ripple’s previously announced goal of achieving full post-quantum readiness by 2028, but provides a more detailed assessment of the work required to reach that target.

Currently, XRP Ledger accounts use secp256k1 or Ed25519 cryptography, both of which could theoretically be compromised by sufficiently advanced quantum computers running Shor’s algorithm.

The concern extends beyond individual XRP wallets. Validators rely on cryptographic signatures to authenticate transactions and coordinate network consensus, while trusted validator list publishers help determine which operators participate in that process.

A successful attack against those systems could allow malicious actors to impersonate legitimate accounts or validators, potentially undermining network security.

The Foundation’s proposal would introduce ML-DSA-44 support throughout these systems, allowing users to migrate before existing cryptographic protections become vulnerable.

However, the upgrade would come with significant technical costs.

According to the research, transactions using the proposed quantum-resistant signatures could consume approximately 5,331 bytes of storage, compared with 1,704 bytes for a conventional payment. That represents an increase of roughly 213%, potentially affecting network bandwidth, transaction history storage, and operating costs.

The Foundation estimates that implementation would require approximately 640 development hours and 400 additional review hours, with projected review, auditing, and related expenses totaling between $215,000 and $255,000, excluding the initial development effort.

The research also identifies unresolved questions around transaction fees, account migration, and compatibility with existing software. Simply adding a quantum-resistant regular key would not fully secure an account if its original vulnerable master key remained enabled.

An implementation has already been tested on the network’s AlphaNet environment, but further development and security reviews are required before deployment.

The roadmap schedules a migration study for the first half of 2027, followed by development, review, and auditing in late 2027 or 2028. No mainnet activation date has been approved.

Ripple previously announced a four-phase quantum security strategy in April, including experimental deployments, contingency planning, and collaboration with security firm Project Eleven. That partnership includes research into hybrid signing systems combining traditional and post-quantum signatures, along with validator testing and custody wallet prototypes.

Blockchains Prepare Post-Quantum Moves

The XRP Ledger is not alone in preparing for the emerging threat.

Bitcoin developers are considering BIP 360, a proposal that would introduce a new output type intended to reduce public-key exposure. Just recently, a longtime Bitcoin Core developer proposed planting secret “quantum landmines” to potentially turn attempted quantum bitcoin thefts into potentially expensive mistakes.

Ethereum has incorporated quantum resistance into its longer-term roadmap, with proposed changes to validator architecture and account authentication targeting broader upgrades around 2029. Solana developers have explored the Falcon post-quantum signature scheme, while Starknet is researching a potential transition from Ethereum Layer 2 to an independent Layer 1 blockchain, partly to gain greater control over its post-quantum security roadmap.

Although no quantum computer has yet demonstrated the ability to break the cryptography securing major blockchains, the XRP Ledger Foundation argues that preparing early is essential because replacing cryptographic systems across a live network could take years.

If successfully deployed, the proposed amendment could position the XRP Ledger among the first major blockchains to support native post-quantum signatures for both ordinary accounts and validators.

title: Poland’s Parliament Votes 240-202 to Let Officials Freeze Crypto Before Court Review
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Poland’s Parliament Votes 240-202 to Let Officials Freeze Crypto Before Court Review
Poland's Sejm passed a sanctions bill Friday that lets the interior minister freeze bitcoin and bank funds of people on a national list, and a court appeal would not pause the freeze.
This post Pol...
content:
Poland’s lower house of parliament voted 240-202 on Friday to let the interior minister freeze crypto assets, bank accounts and other property of people placed on a national sanctions list, before any court reviews the order.

The Sejm, Poland’s lower house, passed the Act on Restrictive Measures at its 68th sitting, with one member abstaining and 17 not voting. The Senate received the bill Monday and has 30 days under Article 121 of the Constitution to adopt, amend or reject it, after which it would go to President Karol Nawrocki.

The law, a government bill that also implements European Union sanctions rules, treats crypto assets as financial means that can be frozen, using the definition in the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation. A freeze, as the text defines it, is meant to stop any movement, transfer, use or other change that would let the holder benefit from the assets.

The freeze applies only to people and entities the interior minister adds to a public national list, either on the minister’s own initiative or at the request of agencies that include the financial watchdog, the central bank, the financial intelligence unit and the internal security service. Grounds include supporting a country already under EU sanctions, serious human rights abuses, or initiating or financing information manipulation that poses a serious threat to Poland’s national security.

A listing on that last ground requires a showing of a real and serious threat to Poland’s interests, borders, security or elections. The bill carves out ordinary journalism, political speech and publishing, unless that activity is a knowing campaign of the kind the law describes.

A freeze that starts before a judge weighs in

The interior minister’s decision takes effect the day after it is posted in the ministry’s Public Information Bulletin and is immediately enforceable. There is no request to the minister to reconsider. A listed person may file a complaint with an administrative court, but the law says the decision remains in force until a judgment becomes final, and it sets aside the usual rule that would let a court pause a challenged order.

The measures also bar making funds or property available to listed persons and can exclude them from public contracts. In some cases, the economy minister may appoint a temporary administrator to sell frozen assets or, under a separate order, take them over for the State Treasury.

What the freeze would mean for bitcoin

The Poland bill does not target ordinary bitcoin holders in Poland. It reaches crypto assets owned, held or under the control of people and firms on the sanctions list. Banks, exchanges and other parties face administrative fines if they fail to freeze those assets or make them available, and compliance is checked by the financial intelligence unit and the Polish Financial Supervision Authority for the firms they already oversee.

The text does not describe a way for officials to obtain the keys to coins held in self-custody. The practical enforcement path in Poland runs through exchanges, custodians and other obliged institutions that can actually stop a transfer.

What comes next for the bill

The bill still has to clear the Senate and Nawrocki’s desk. The president refused to sign a separate crypto-assets market bill the Sejm passed on May 15, and lawmakers in September failed to override that veto, voting 241-198. He had also vetoed earlier versions of that market bill, arguing the rules went too far.

That earlier fight was about licensing and supervision under the EU’s crypto-assets rulebook, not about a sanctions freeze. Whether the Senate trims the pre-court freeze, and whether Nawrocki will sign a sanctions law that reaches bitcoin, is the question the bill now leaves open.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

Then, to facilitate these transactions, the platform has a blockchain-based token, Binance Coin (BNB), and offers discounts to users who pay using this native cryptocurrency token. Apart from these features, Binance has an In-App NFT marketplace, a comprehensive learning platform, and opportunities for users to earn passive income. 

The platform is designed to handle 1.4 million transactions every single second, so you don’t have to worry about lag during busy market moves. The ecosystem also includes a venture capital arm and a massive educational portal called “Binance Academy” to help you learn.
