Join over 300 million global users — create your Binance account today and start trading with 0.1% fees.

Binance Global vs Binance US

The main difference between Binance Global and Binance US is that they are actually separate legal entities that follow different sets of rules. 

You can use the global Binance platform version if you live outside the United States, and it has the full list of over 500 coins and high-leverage futures. The US version is built specifically for American residents to meet the strict requirements of US financial regulators. Well, because of these strict laws, the US platform has fewer coins (around 150) and does not offer derivatives like futures or options trading.

Also, on Binance Global, you can easily deposit and withdraw dozens of fiat currencies through bank transfers, credit or debit cards, and third‑party payment services. Binance US currently does not offer cash deposits or withdrawals (limited only). US users rely on ACH transfers and wire transfers for limited fiat support, and these may carry higher fees.

How Does Binance Work?

The Binance platform works by acting as a middleman that connects people who want to buy crypto with people who want to sell it. You can easily create an account, deposit funds, and then you use the exchange’s order book to place your trades. The system then uses its matching engine to pair your buy order with someone else’s sell order at the best possible price. Once the trade is complete, the assets are transferred between internal wallets.

You will notice that your account is divided into several sub-wallets based on what you are doing. You have a Spot Wallet for regular buying and holding, a Futures Wallet for leverage trading, and an Earn Wallet for your savings. You can move your money between these wallets instantly and for free. Basically, this structure helps you keep your different trading strategies organized so you don’t accidentally spend your long-term savings on a risky day trade.

What are the Pros and Cons of Binance Exchanges?

The pros of Binance include support for 500+ cryptocurrencies, competitive fees, advanced trading features, and strong security. While, the cons of the Binance exchange are the Binance US version for Americans with fewer features, overwhelming for beginners, and regulatory issues in the past. 

Advantages of Binance

  • 500+ Listed Cryptocurrencies to Choose From: Binance Exchange offers more than 500 tradable coins for all its customers. This gives crypto traders and investors many options. They can decide to trade or buy popular tokens, meme coins, GameFi, and even AI coins. But if you are in the United States using Binance.US, you have fewer options, around 150 coins to choose from.
  • Multiple Trading Pairs: Binance has over 1,300 trading pairs from which traders can choose. Some of these pairs include BTC/USDT, BTC/FDUSD, XRP/USDT, ETH/USDT,  USDC/USDT, SOL/USDT, and many more.
  • Competitive Fees: Compared to other crypto exchanges like Coinbase or Kraken, Binance offers low trading fees (0.1% maker/taker), so you don’t have to worry about paying a significant portion of your investments and earnings on transaction fees. Additionally, you can get 25% discounts if you use the Binance coin, BNB.
  • Multiple Trading Options and Order Types: Binance Exchange offers various trading options, including peer-to-peer, margin, and spot trading. The platform also has many order types, including limit order, market order, stop-limit order, stop market order, trailing stop order, and post-only order.
  • Robust Security and KYC: Binance enforces various security measures to protect users. For instance, the platform requires a strong password during registration and 2FA for all sensitive operations, such as logging in and transferring funds. They also encrypt data in storage and in transit to ensure that only you can access your personal information. Plus, in addition to these measures, Binance has a strict Know-Your-Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) policy.
  • Supports Fiat-to-crypto: Binance users can easily convert their local currency into digital assets. Some supported fiat on Binance include GBP, AUD, BRL, EUR, USD, ZAR, and RUS. You can make these fiat-to-crypto deposits using bank transfers, online banking, e-wallets, credit/debit cards, and Google/Apple Pay.
  • User-Friendly Mobile app: The Binance app is available for iOS and Android with a simplified Lite mode for beginners and an advanced Pro mode for traders. The app also integrates the Web3 wallet, NFTs, and Earn features.

Want access to 500+ cryptocurrencies and advanced trading tools? Register your Binance account now and start trading in minutes.

Disadvantages of Binance

  • Binance US is Limited: Binance US is a separate exchange operating under different regulations for Binance traders in the United States. Due to these strict regulations, the platform is more limited than the global exchange. It supports about 150 coins and 170+ trading pairs. It was established in 2019, and it is only available in 38 states; traders in Hawaii, Texas, New York, and Vermont cannot use the platform. Also, you cannot trade futures or invest with a margin account on Binance.US.
  • Binance Exchange May be Confusing for New Users: Binance offers advanced trading features, multiple supported cryptocurrencies, and Web3 services. While this may be exciting for experienced traders, it can be confusing for people who are new to the crypto space. In fact, even traders who are familiar with the platform might feel overwhelmed due to all the options available.
  • Lawsuits and Regulatory Trouble in Multiple Countries: Binance has faced many regulatory and legal issues in multiple countries. In November 2023, Binance and its CEO, CZ, pleaded guilty to unlicensed money transmitting and anti-money laundering violations charges. This happened a month after Binance paused all U.S. dollar deposits, withdrawals, and trades in response to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) lawsuit filed against Binance.US on June 5, 2023.
  • Custodial Risk: Although Binance offers self‑custody through its Web3 wallet, most of the users keep their funds on the exchange for trading. In November 2022 and October 2023, there were hacks against the BNB Chain (around $570 million), and earlier in 2019, hackers stole about 7,000 BTC from the exchange. Obviously, Binance covered the losses through the SAFU fund, but these incidents eventually show that even big exchanges are not immune to security breaches.

Who Is Binance Best For?

Binance is best for active day traders, altcoin investors, passive income, high-volume traders, and tech-savvy beginners.

  • Active traders: People who trade often and require deep liquidity, low fees, and sophisticated tools. You see, the large selection of pairs, high leverage, and advanced order types can easily attract day traders and professional investors.
  • Altcoin enthusiasts: Generally, those looking to buy or sell lesser‑known cryptocurrencies or take part in new token launches through the Launchpad will find more options on Binance than on most competitors.
  • Yield seekers: If you want to earn passive income on your crypto, Binance offers numerous staking, lending, and yield farming products with competitive returns.
  • High‑volume traders: VIP tier programs reward high trading volumes with lower fees and better borrowing rates. Plus, corporations or trading firms can also open institutional accounts with dedicated support and portfolio margin programs.
  • Tech‑savvy beginners: It has the Lite interface and educational resources like Binance Academy, so new users can start with simple buys and gradually explore more advanced products.

If Binance fits your trading goals, open your account today and activate your referral bonus before placing your first trade.

What are Binance Fees?

The Binance fees include spot trading charges (0.1% maker/taker), futures trading fees (0.02% maker, 0.05% taker), zero deposit fees, and variable withdrawal fees (depending on the network).

Deposit Fees

The platform generally does not charge you any fees to deposit cryptocurrency into your account. You only have to pay the network fee to the blockchain when you send the coins from your personal wallet.  Unlike crypto deposits, fiat deposits involve third-party payment providers. The table below summarizes the core fees for retail users (both crypto and fiat deposit fees):

Deposit methodBinance Global
Bank transfer (SEPA, FPS, ACH)Free for most currencies. SEPA bank deposit is usually free; Faster Payments Service (FPS) in the UK is free.
Debit/credit cardCard deposits cost around 1.8-2% of the amount. Apple Pay and Google Pay have similar rates
Third‑party payments (Simplex, Banxa, etc.)Fees vary by service, typically around 1-3%
Crypto depositFree; network miners’ fee paid by sender

Withdrawal Fees

Binance crypto withdrawal fees are not fixed, and they change based on which coin you are moving and how busy the network is. You will find that withdrawing Bitcoin usually costs a $5-$10, but withdrawing tokens on the BNB Chain (previously Binance Smart Chain) or Solana can cost less than 50 cents. Actually, the exchange updates these rates regularly to make sure they match the actual blockchain costs.

Withdrawal methodBinance Global
Bank transferSEPA withdrawals cost around €1-€1.50; wire transfers cost $15; some regions are free.
Debit/credit cardNot available for withdrawals.
Crypto withdrawalOnly the network fee is charged

Spot Trading Fees

Binance spot trading charges are based on a tiered system, from regular users to VIP 9. Now, for regular users, a 0.10% maker and taker fee is charged for spot trading. 

Your fees reduce slightly if you are trading USDC. Makers still pay the standard rate, but takers pay 0.095%. If you increase your trading volume over 30 days or hold a significant amount of BNB in your account, your spot trading fees will drop to as low as 0.011% / 0.023% maker-taker. (check screenshot below for exact discount details and VIP tiers)

Futures Trading Fees

Futures trading has a separate fee schedule because the volumes are usually much larger than spot trading. Makers, who provide liquidity to the book, pay as little as 0.02%, while takers pay around 0.05%. You also get a 10% discount on futures fees if you pay using your BNB balance. Right now, these are some of the lowest derivatives fees you can find on any major centralized exchange.

Margin Trading Fees

Binance margin trading has two cost components: trading commission (same as spot rates) and interest on borrowed funds. These rates change every single day based on how many people are borrowing that specific coin. Generally, USDT interest rates might be around 5% to 10% per year, while smaller altcoins might be much more expensive.

Staking and Earn Fees

The Binance platform does not usually charge a direct fee for you to participate in staking or the Earn programs. But instead, the company takes a small percentage of the rewards that the blockchain pays out before they give you your share. So, this means the APY (Annual Percentage Yield) you see in the app is the net amount you will actually receive. Binance.US, however, deducts a 9.95% to 39.95% service fee from staking rewards.

What Are the Best Features of Binance?

The best features of the Binance exchange are advanced trading features, staking services, launchpad, user-friendly mobile app, passive income options, web3 wallet, cloud mining, and an NFT marketplace. 

Binance Trading Features

The top Binance trading features are spot trading, margin trading, futures trading, options trading, copy trading, and automated trading bots.

Binance Margin Trading

Binance margin trading allows you to borrow funds to increase your position size. Binance offers isolated margin (up to 10x leverage), where the collateral is tied to one trading pair, and cross margin (up to 5x). There is also cross margin pro for institutional and high‑volume users that raises leverage to 20x. Higher leverage increases both potential profits and losses.

Here, margin loans generally accrue interest every hour, and rates depend on the coin you borrow (as discussed earlier). Binance also uses a “Smart Liquidation” engine that gradually reduces your positions instead of closing them all at once. There is also Portfolio Margin. It lets you use combined balances across spot, margin, and futures to lower margin requirements and support large leveraged trades.

Binance Spot Trading

Binance spot trading means you can buy and sell crypto directly with market or limit orders. Spot trading pairs include crypto‑crypto pairs (e.g., BTC/ETH), crypto‑fiat pairs (e.g., ETH/EUR), and stablecoin pairs (e.g., BNB/USDT). 

The interface allows you to view order book depth, price charts, and trade history. Generally, spot trades settle immediately, and you own the underlying asset.

Now, if you are a more advanced trader, Binance provides more advanced features for the spot market to support order types and charting features. These features allow you to set limits, market, stop-limit orders, and more. You can read our in-depth Binance spot trading review for more info.

Binance Futures Trading

Binance futures trading lets you bet on whether the price of a coin will go up or down without actually owning the coin itself. It offers USDT‑margined perpetual contracts, coin‑margined perpetual contracts, and delivery futures with expiry dates. 

You can use much higher leverage here, sometimes up to 125x for certain pairs. Binance also provides tools such as isolated and cross margin for futures, take‑profit and stop‑loss orders, bracket orders, and a risk calculator. Check out our Binance futures review article for more details.

Binance Options Trading

Binance options trading gives you the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell a coin at a certain price before a certain date. You can trade European‑style options settled in USDT, and these options have a set strike price and expiry time. The platform has a very simplified options interface that makes it easier to understand than the ones used in traditional stock markets. 

Now, because they are European options, you cannot exercise early, and the platform also offers a simple options widget called “Vanilla Options” for beginner use. 

Binance Copy Trading

Binance copy trading allows you to follow the strategies of other experienced traders. Basically, you can choose a lead trader, allocate funds, and then the system automatically mirrors their trades. 

Here, lead traders earn a 10-30 % share of the profits, and they must maintain consistent performance to remain in the program. You can copy in two ways: fixed amount, where you invest a specific sum, and fixed ratio, where your position sizes follow the same ratio as the lead trader’s positions. 

There is also an “Elite Trader Program” that requires at least 300 copy traders and $750,000 in assets under management. Copy trading supports both spot and futures markets. Also, you can stop copying at any time and withdraw your funds. There are no restrictions.

Binance Trading Bot

Binance offers built-in bots that can trade for you 24/7 based on rules you set. Here are some top Binance trading bots:

  • Spot Grid Bot: This one can place buy and sell orders around a set price range, profiting from sideways markets by buying low and selling high.
  • Futures Grid Bot: Similar to spot grid but for perpetual contracts. So, it will use leverage.
  • Arbitrage Bot: It will exploit price differences between funding rates or futures and spot prices.
  • Rebalancing Bot: This bot generally keeps your portfolio balanced by periodically adjusting allocations to maintain target ratios. You can set the coins and percentage distribution, and the bot rebalances at regular intervals or when price thresholds are met.
  • Auto‑Invest Bot: Implements dollar cost averaging by automatically buying selected coins at fixed intervals. You can choose daily, weekly, or monthly frequency and have the option to earn interest on unspent stablecoins.
  • Spot DCA Bot: This bot buys increments of a coin when the price drops by a set percentage and sells increments when the price rises by a set percentage. It helps manage volatility.
  • Futures TWAP/VP Bots: The bot will execute large orders over time using time‑weighted average price (TWAP) or volume participation (VP) strategies to minimize market impact.

Binance Staking

Binance staking allows you to earn rewards just by holding certain coins in your account. The platform handles all the technical work, and you just click a button to start earning interest. You can choose “Locked Staking” for higher returns if you don’t mind locking your coins there for a set time, or “Flexible Staking” if you want to be able to withdraw them whenever you want.

Binance takes a 10% cut of rewards on popular coins such as Ethereum and Solana. There is also ETH 2.0 liquid staking, which provides a token called WBETH that represents your staked ETH and accrues staking rewards. Explore our Binance staking review article for more info. 

Binance Launchpad

Binance Launchpad is a platform for new cryptocurrency projects to raise capital through token sales. You can participate by holding BNB in your account. The number of tokens you can buy depends on your average BNB holdings over a snapshot period (often 7–30 days) and the project’s allocation rules. 

Binance calculates your ticket based on hourly snapshots of your BNB balance, and at the end of the subscription period, winning tickets are drawn, and BNB is deducted from your wallet to purchase the new tokens. Check out our full Binance launchpad review here.

Binance Mobile App

The Binance mobile app offers two modes: Lite for beginners and Pro for experienced traders. The Lite version displays simple buy/sell options, price charts, and a portfolio overview. The Pro version provides full order books, margin and futures trading, advanced charting, and access to copy trading, bots, and Earn. 

The app also integrates with the Web3 wallet, so you can access DeFi and NFTs within the same interface. It has all the top security features, like biometric login (fingerprint/face), device management, anti‑phishing codes, and the ability to freeze your account from the app.

Binance Earn

Binance Earn is basically a high-yield savings account for your crypto. You can put your coins into various products like “Simple Earn” or “Dual Investment” to get a better return than just letting them HODL in your wallet. Now, within Earn, you will find:

  • Simple Earn: Flexible and locked staking as explained earlier.
  • Launchpool: You can stake BNB or stablecoins to farm new tokens.
  • Dual Investment: You can earn a fixed yield by committing crypto or stablecoins to a price target. Here, if the price is above the target at expiry, you receive your crypto plus yield in stablecoins; if below, you receive more crypto plus yield. It suits users comfortable with market exposure.

Binance Web3 Wallet

Binance Web3 Wallet is a self‑custodial cryptocurrency wallet built into the Binance mobile app. The wallet uses multi‑party computation (MPC). Here, your private key is split into multiple shares. So, one share stays on your device, one stays on Binance’s servers, and the last one is saved in your personal cloud (such as iCloud or Google Drive). 

Now, you need at least two shares to sign a transaction, so neither you nor Binance can move funds alone. The wallet supports multiple blockchains, including BNB Chain, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, and more. It also has a dApp browser so you can interact with DeFi, yield farms, NFT platforms, and games within the app. Here is the full Binance Web3 wallet review.

Binance Cloud Mining

Binance cloud mining allows you to earn Bitcoin (BTC) without having to buy expensive mining hardware yourself. You basically rent the “hash power” from the platform’s massive data centers, and they send the rewards to your account every day. This is a great way to get into mining if you live in a place where electricity is expensive or if you don’t have space for loud machines. You can read our in-depth Binance cloud mining review to know more.

Binance NFT Marketplace

Binance has its own marketplace where you can buy, sell, and even create your own Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs). You can find digital art, gaming items, and collectibles from creators all over the world. The platform supports BEP‑721 and BEP‑1155 standards on the BNB Chain. You can check out the full Binance NFT marketplace review for more details.

How to Open a Trading Account at Binance Global Exchange?

Step 1: Click the “Open Account” button below to start Binance or download the Binance app, and register your Binance account using your email address, mobile phone number, Google account, or Apple ID.

Step 2: Check the “agree with Binance terms of service and privacy policy”, and click “Next” to proceed. Binance will then send a verification code to the email or phone number you added. Enter the code number and click Submit.

Step 3: At this step, you need to create a strong password (at least 8 characters, including uppercase letters and numbers).

Step 4: If you didn’t use the registration link in step one, add our Binance referral code here manually to get rewards. This code can give you up to $100 in a free crypto sign-up bonus. After that, Binance will ask you to complete your verification. Click “Continue” to start the verification process.

Step 5: Finally, once you finish the KYC verification process, it can generally take a few hours to two days to have your account verified and ready for use.

Follow the steps above and register your Binance account now to claim up to $100 in crypto rewards.

How to Deposit to Your Binance Trading Account?

To deposit fiat on Binance, you need to go to the “Deposit” section, choose your local currency, select a payment method, enter the amount, and wait for confirmation.

To deposit crypto on Binance, you need to select the cryptocurrency, copy the deposit address, and send the funds from your external wallet.

Fiat Deposits

  • Choose your currency: Log in, go to Wallet > Fiat and Spot > Deposit, then select your local currency (USD, EUR, GBP, INR, etc.).
  • Select a payment method: You can choose bank transfer (SEPA, SWIFT, ACH, FPS), card deposit, or third‑party services. Now, for example, if you are in India, you might use IMPS or a UPI transfer; in Europe, you would use SEPA; in the US, you can use ACH or a debit card (available only on Binance US).
  • Enter the amount: Now, you need to type how much you want to deposit and follow the instructions to complete the transfer. Here, for card deposits, you will be redirected to the payment processor, and bank transfers require you to send money to a Binance bank account with your reference code.
  • Wait for confirmation: Generally, bank transfers may take hours or days; card deposits are instant. Once funds arrive, you will see them in your Fiat and Spot wallet.

Crypto Deposits

  • Choose the crypto: Go to Wallet > Fiat and Spot > Deposit, then select your desired coin (e.g., BTC, ETH, USDT).
  • Select network: Binance generally supports multiple networks for many coins, so for instance, USDT can be deposited via Ethereum (ERC‑20), BNB Chain (BEP‑20), Tron (TRC‑20), or Arbitrum. 
  • Copy the deposit address: Binance generates an address, so you need to copy it and paste it into the sending wallet. Also, some coins require a memo or tag (e.g., for XRP, XLM), and if you forget the memo, your deposit may be delayed. So, check that too.
  • Send the funds: Now, you can initiate the transfer from your external wallet, and after network confirmations, the deposit will appear in your Binance wallet. Well, deposits are usually credited after one or two confirmations for major coins; smaller networks may take longer.

How to Trade on Binance?

To trade on Binance, you can start with the “Convert” feature if you want to swap coins without looking at charts, and for more control, you should use the “Spot Trading” interface, which gives you access to the full order book.

  • Find the “Trade” menu and select “Spot.”
  • Search for the pair you want to trade, like BTC/USDT, on the right side of the screen.
  • Choose between a “Market” order to buy immediately at the current price or a “Limit” order to set your own price.
  • Enter the amount of crypto you want to buy and click the large green “Buy” button. Actually, you can also set “Stop-Loss” orders to protect your money if you think the price may drop too fast.

How to Withdraw from Binance?

To withdraw from Binance, go to the “withdraw” section, choose coin, paste the withdrawal address, select the network and amount, and finally confirm the transaction. 

  • Navigate to your wallet and select the “Withdraw” option.
  • Enter the destination address of your private wallet and pick the matching network.
  • Type in the amount of crypto you want to move.
  • Confirm the transaction and wait for the blockchain to process it. Generally, most withdrawals take between 5 and 20 minutes to complete.

What are the Available Cryptocurrencies on Binance?

There are currently over 500 cryptocurrencies available on Binance. You can generally find everything from the top-rated coins that everyone knows to small experimental projects (mostly on Binance Alpha).

  • Top Assets: You can trade Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and Solana (SOL) with massive volume.
  • Stablecoins: The platform supports USDT, USDC, and its own FDUSD stablecoin for safekeeping.
  • Ecosystem Tokens: You can buy BNB, which powers the entire ecosystem and gives you fee discounts.
  • Meme Coins: You can find popular tokens like DOGE, PEPE, and SHIB listed with high liquidity.
  • DeFi and AI Coins: The exchange lists hundreds of project tokens for Artificial Intelligence and decentralized finance.

Binance Security Review: Is It a Safe and Legit Crypto Exchange to Trade?

Yes, Binance is a legit and safe crypto exchange. It uses industry‑standard security measures and has a large insurance fund. Here are its most advanced security systems:

  • Proof of Reserves (PoR): Binance publishes Merkle tree proofs showing that the exchange holds reserves equal to users’ balances. So, you can verify your own balances on the PoR page by generating a leaf of the Merkle tree, and the audit covers major assets like BTC, ETH, USDT, and BNB.
  • Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU): Binance created the SAFU in 2018. It is an insurance fund seeded with trading fees and acts as a backstop in case of hacks or extreme events. Currently, at the time of writing, Binance converted SAFU holdings to BTC, worth about $1 billion. The company pledged to top up the fund if its value falls below $800 million.
  • Cold storage: The majority of user funds on Binance are kept in cold wallets not connected to the internet, and only a small portion remains in hot wallets for daily withdrawals.
  • Risk engine: Binance uses an automated risk engine to monitor accounts and block suspicious activity. Basically, it includes real‑time transaction monitoring, geofencing, and anti‑money laundering (AML) procedures.
  • Withdrawal whitelisting: Binance also has an address whitelisting feature that restricts withdrawals to only pre-approved addresses. When you enable this feature, your account can only send funds to these whitelisted addresses. This will prevent unauthorized access and losses in a phishing attack or hack.

Trade with confidence on a platform backed by Proof of Reserves and a $1B SAFU fund — create your Binance account today.

But yes, Binance has also faced many regulatory issues in various countries. But besides regulatory issues, it has also been involved in scandals and significant lawsuits, like the one filed against Binance.US by the SEC in June 2023. 

Also, Binance and its CEO, Changpeng Zhao, pleaded guilty to anti-money laundering violations and other charges on November 21, 2023. Binance agreed to pay $4.3 billion to settle charges, while Changpeng Zhao stepped down as CEO and agreed to pay $50 million toward the settlement.

Can Binance be Trusted?

Yes, the Binance exchange can be trusted because it has a long history of protecting users and following international financial standards. You might hear about legal battles in the news, but the company has always worked with governments to resolve these issues and improve its systems. 

There are over 300 million registered users globally without any problems, which is obviously a very strong sign of reliability. Actually, the company has survived many “crypto winters” and market crashes while remaining the number one exchange in the world. But still, it’s a custodial platform. So, we say, use Binance for trading and short‑term storage, then transfer your long‑term holdings to a personal hardware wallet you control.

content:
Binance trading bots are automated trading tools that execute trades for users based on predefined strategies. These bots operate 24/7 and are designed to make crypto trading more efficient, reduce emotional decision-making, and take advantage of market opportunities that traders may miss while inactive or during manual trading.

To ensure precision, Binance automated trading bots can collect market data, analyze it, and execute trades based on preset strategies and collated data within milliseconds. As the name implies, these bots are provided by Binance, a global cryptocurrency exchange that allows investors to buy, hold, sell, and trade crypto coins and non-fungible tokens (NFTs) in one place.

On Binance, traders can access eight crypto bots designed to execute different trading strategies automatically. Keep reading this Binance crypto trading bot review to learn more about trading bots for Binance, the fees for using Binance bots, and how to set up a trading bot on Binance.

  • How to Set up a Trading Bot on Binance?

    • Are Binance Trading Bots Safe and Legal?
    • What are the Risks of Using Binance Automated Trading Bots?
    • Do Binance Trading Bots Guarantee Profits?

What is Binance Trading Bot?

Binance trading bots are advanced tools that help investors trade cryptocurrencies automatically on the Binance exchange. These bots use preset rules to analyze market trends, monitor prices, and place buy or sell orders without human supervision. Binance offers eight trading bots, each designed to suit a particular strategy or market condition.

Instead of placing every trade yourself or managing many positions simultaneaously, a Binance trading bot can carry out tasks like buying low and selling high (grid bots), maintaining a specific investment ratio (rebalancing bots), executing large trades over time (TWAP or VP bots), or even gradually building a position over time (DCA bots).

These bots are built directly into the Binance platform, which means users don’t need third-party software or coding skills to get started. Once configured, the bot follows the rules the user sets and trades continuously, even when the trader is offline.

Set up a bot trading account on Binance and receive $100 plus up to total 30% discount on spot and trading fees.

What Are the Pros and Cons of Binance Trading Bot?

The pros of the Binance trading bot are listed below:

  • 24/7 Trading: Like other crypto bots, Binance trading bots do not need rest. These advanced trading tools are designed to keep watching the market, open positions, and manage trades around the clock, so you won’t miss any opportunities when you are away from your screen.
  • No Emotional Trading: Often, emotions like fear, greed, impatience, or excitement lead to poor trading decisions. Bots strictly follow programmed logic, which means they don’t panic during sudden price drops or get greedy during rallies. This helps maintain discipline and stick to your initial trading strategy.
  • Faster Trade Execution: One major reason traders deploy bots for seamless crypto trading experience is the execution speed. Bots can open positions, modify, and cancel orders faster than humans. They can monitor dozens of trading pairs simultaneously and execute multiple trades within seconds.
  • Backtesting Trading Strategies: Many bots let you backtest your strategy using historical data. This means you can see how it would have performed in the past before risking your funds.
  • Customization Options: Binance bots offer a range of strategies tailored to different market conditions. Whether you’re trying to place simple buy and sell orders and profit from price fluctuations or reduce entry risk over time, there’s a bot for nearly every trading style. This gives you control over how the bot trades, based on your goals and risk level.

The cons of the Binance trading bot are listed below:

  • Not Beginner-Friendly: Even though you don’t need to code or be an advanced trader, a basic understanding of trading concepts like stop-loss, leverage, volatility, and risk management is necessary. You could risk more than intended if you don’t understand what the bot is doing.
  • You Can Still Lose Money: Bots follow rules, but they don’t guarantee profits. If markets move against your strategy or you configure the bot poorly (e.g., wrong price range), you can suffer significant losses. Additionally, trading with leverage-based bots, like those for the futures market, is even riskier than spot-based bots.
  • Requires Monitoring and Strategy Adjustments: Although bots are automated, you still need to monitor them, especially during sudden market crashes, exchange issues, or liquidity changes. If you completely ignore the Binance trading bots, they could keep executing trades based on outdated parameters.

What Are the Types of Binance Automated Trading Bots?

The types of Binance automated trading bots are Spot Grid, Futures Grid, Arbitrage bot, Rebalancing bot, Algo Order, Futures TWAP, Futures VP, and Spot DCA. Here is a breakdown of the different trading strategies these advanced trading tools execute.

  1. Spot Grid

The Spot Grid automates trading in the spot market by placing a series of buy and sell orders at predefined price intervals. This grid bot is built for market conditions where prices move sideways within a specific range instead of up and down. The goal is to buy an asset at lower levels and sell it when it moves higher, making small profits from market fluctuations.

  1. Futures Grid

This bot is similar to Spot Grid but is applied to the futures market instead of the spot market. It allows traders to go long or short and even apply leverage. The Futures Grid is perfect for traders who want to profit from price movements in both directions while taking advantage of up to 125x leverage to potentially increase their returns.

  1. Arbitrage Bot (Futures Funding Rate Arbitrage)

The Arbitrage Bot takes advantage of price differences between trading pairs or across different markets (spot and futures) to profit from funding fees. Simply put, the Arbitrage bot allows traders to hedge their positions in the futures market by taking an opposite position for the same trading pair in the spot market.

If you decide to use this bot, you will be opening both long and short positions in different markets to profit from either market and collect funding rates. If you incur a loss on the open position in the futures market, you can offset it with the profit you make in the spot market and vice versa.

  1. Rebalancing Bot

The Rebalancing Bot automatically adjusts your portfolio position in your selected token combination to ensure you maintain the same ratio among a group of selected assets. For example, if you want to keep a 50/50 balance between Bitcoin and Ethereum, the Rebalancing Bot will monitor price changes and adjust the holdings automatically by buying or selling to maintain that ratio.

Institutional and long-term traders often use this not for portfolio management, but for active trading. It manages risks by spreading your capital across various cryptos, helps you stick to your crypto trading goals, and potentially increases returns by selling overvalued assets and buying undervalued ones.

Join Binance today and get an additional 20% discount on all your trading fees.

  1. Algo Order (TWAP & POV Strategies)

The Spot Algo Order helps traders execute large orders and potentially illiquid trades without significantly impacting the market. Instead of placing one massive order that could cause slippage or unfavourable price movements, this bot breaks the order into smaller parts and spreads them out over time based on a selected automated trading algorithm.

Binance offers two types of algorithmic orders: Time-weighted Average Price (TWAP) and Percentage of Volume (POV). TWAP is a time-based algo bot that monitors the order book and executes small portions of the total order at regular intervals throughout the specified duration to minimize market impact and reduce slippage.

Meanwhile, the POV algo bot is percentage-based, executing trades based on a specified percentage of the total market trading volume. The execution rate of a POV algo order depends on market volume or activity. When market activity is high, the order executes faster; when volume decreases, execution slows down, maintaining a consistent participation rate.

  1. Futures TWAP

The Futures TWAP bot disperses large futures orders into smaller quantities and places them gradually over a set period to get better execution prices. This bot aims to achieve an average execution price that reflects the time-based average of market prices specified by the trader.

The futures TWAP bot is useful when trying to enter or exit a position without causing noticeable price disruption, especially in less liquid markets. If you are considering using the futures TWAP bot, Binance supports it on USD-M Futures contracts via API and through the futures trading bots interface.

  1. Futures VP

The Futures Volume Participation (VP) bot is designed to execute trades based on the level of market activity. Instead of fixed time intervals like with TWAP, VP executes orders proportionally to the current market trading volume. When market volume is high, the order executes faster; when volume is low, execution slows down. This helps maintain a steady market participation rate and reduces the risk of moving the market price.

  1. Spot DCA

The Spot DCA (Dollar-Cost Averaging) bot helps investors buy or sell a fixed amount of cryptocurrency assets at regular intervals or when the price changes by a predetermined percentage.

The bot buys more of the asset when the market price falls below your initial purchase price, aiming to lower your average buy cost. It continues buying until the price rises above your preset take-profit percentage, at which point it sells the asset to lock in profits.

How do Binance Trading Bots Work?

Binance trading bots work by following predefined strategies and parameters to automatically execute trades on the Binance platform. Users configure the bot with specific rules such as price ranges, order sizes, price deviation percentages, take-profit targets, and order frequency.

The bot then automatically places buy or sell orders according to these settings. Once activated, the bot continuously monitors the market and executes trades according to the strategy, whether it is grid trading, dollar-cost averaging (DCA), arbitrage, or other supported strategies.

This automation ensures your trades happen promptly and consistently, even when you are offline. Another standout feature of Binance bot trading is that the Bot Marketplace allows users to discover and replicate top bot strategies created by experienced traders, making it easier for beginners to start automated trading without creating strategies from scratch.

What Are the Rules For Automated Binance Trading Bots?

The rules for automated Binance trading bots are explained below:

  1. API Access & Permissions: To use a bot on Binance, you need to create an API key directly from your account settings. This Binance API key allows the bot to interact with your account and carry out trades on your behalf. You can decide the bot’s permissions, whether reading your data or actively placing trades. For security reasons, it’s best to turn withdrawal permissions off.
  2. Technical and Trading Limits: To maintain system stability, Binance sets technical limits, such as rate limits on order submissions (e.g., a maximum of 10 orders per second on Binance Futures). It also limits how many times your bot can make API calls within a specific time frame.

If your bot sends too many requests too quickly, Binance might temporarily block it. This helps keep the system fair and stable for everyone using the platform. So, ensure your bot is programmed to stay within the allowed rate limits.

  1. Security Compliance: Never share your API key with anyone, and avoid storing it in places that aren’t secure. Hackers often target bots with poor security setups, so it’s important to protect your trading credentials. Even if your bot is reliable, one security breach can wipe out your funds. Always use two-factor authentication and regularly check your bot’s access settings.
  2. KYC & Regional Restrictions: Before you start Binance bot trading, you must complete Binance’s KYC verification process. This ensures that all users are identified and meet local compliance rules. Also, if you’re in a region where the Binance global platform can’t operate, including the US, you cannot bypass restrictions and use the bot.
  3. Compliance with Terms of Use: All automated trading activity must follow Binance’s terms of use and any other policies they update over time. If your bot violates any terms, the exchange reserves the right to freeze and restrict your account, which will affect your Binance bot trading account.

What Are the Fees for Using Trading Bot on Binance?

When using Binance’s trading bots, there is no extra fee specifically for the bot itself; the service is built-in at no additional cost. This means you can take advantage of automated strategies using a Binance trading bot free of charge without paying anything extra beyond your usual trading expenses.

However, you still incur the normal trading fees when transactions are executed. For example, on the Spot market, the cost is around 0.1% for makers and takers, so you must pay the standard trading fees. For Futures trading, the fees are about 0.02% for makers and 0.04% for takers. Fortunately, these fees can drop to 0.075% if you use BNB for fee payments or reach a higher VIP level with a higher 30-day trading volume.

How to Set up a Trading Bot on Binance?

To set up a trading bot on Binance, you’ll first need to create a Binance account and fund it. Step 1: Visit the Binance official website, provide the information required, add a current Binance referral code to be eligible for bonuses, and complete the KYC verification process. 

Get 100 USDT for free and other exclusive rewards in welcome bonuses to fund your bot trades.

Step 2: Once you’ve registered, log in to your Binance account, go to the (Trade) menu, and then go to (Trading Bots). Read the terms carefully. If you agree, check the box and then click “Confirm” to continue.

Step 3: Next, you will see the trading bot landing page. Click “Trade Now,” and the system will take you to the trading page.

Step 4: You will find different trading bots at the top. Choose the one you wish to create and set your parameters. You will need details like the trading pair, your order type, the amount you wish to trade, etc. After setting the parameters, click Start. The bot will automatically place buy and sell orders within the specified range.

Is Binance Trading Bot Profitable?

Yes, Binance trading bots can be profitable, but it depends on how you use them. Their success comes down to your trading strategy, setting the bot up correctly, and how well you monitor the bot’s performance. If you’re exploring options beyond Binance, you might also want to check out some of the best crypto trading bots available on the market.

Does Binance Have a Trading Bot?

Yes, Binance has about eight trading bots that automate your trades. These bots are designed for different traders and strategies, but they generally allow you to set up strategies for spot trading, futures, and algorithmic trading. Once set, the bots carry out trades based on the conditions you define. This helps you manage your investments without being active all the time.

Are Binance Trading Bots Safe and Legal?

Binance trading bots are safe and legal. Using Binance trading bots can only become illegal if you use them against the company’s terms and conditions or in countries where Binance is banned.

Binance itself is a trusted exchange licensed in many countries. The trading platform also implements strong security measures, such as cold storage for users’ funds, a separate fund to reimburse victims of security breaches, and a bug bounty program to help catch vulnerabilities early.

What are the Risks of Using Binance Automated Trading Bots?

Binance automated trading bots can make trading easier and profitable, but they also come with risks. It is essential to understand these products before using them. The risks of using Binance automated trading bots are technical issues, market volatility, overtrading, dependency on strategy, regulatory concerns, lack of human oversight, and over-reliance.

  1. Technical Issues: Bots can experience glitches or connection problems, leading to missed trades or incorrect actions. If the bot’s code isn’t well-written, it can result in unexpected behaviour, which can cause significant losses if you’re not monitoring its performance.
  2. Market Volatility: Bots don’t have the flexibility to adjust to changes in market sentiment. They are programmed with fixed strategies that can’t adapt quickly to sudden market shifts. They might make trades based on outdated signals in volatile markets, leading to losses. 
  3. Overtrading: Some bots, like the Grid bots, are set to execute trades frequently, which can lead to excessive transaction fees. If the bot isn’t programmed to avoid overtrading, it might take on more risk than you intended.
  4. Dependency on Strategy: Bots follow a set strategy, which might not be effective in all market conditions. If the strategy becomes outdated or isn’t suited to current trends, the bot will struggle because it can’t improvise or adjust to unforeseen circumstances.
  5. Regulatory Risks: Different countries have laws regarding cryptocurrency trading, and bots can sometimes fall into grey areas. Using an automated bot without considering local regulations could lead to legal issues. You could face fines or account restrictions if a bot violates your country’s rules.
  6. Lack of Human Oversight: Bots operate 24/7 without human intervention. If something goes wrong, you might not catch it immediately, leading to substantial losses. Without oversight, it’s easy to miss key changes in the market.
  7. Over-reliance on Bots: Relying solely on bots can prevent you from gaining valuable experience as a trader. Bots follow predefined strategies and don’t help you learn to read the market. Over time, you might lose the skills needed to trade effectively on your own. So, it is essential to balance using bots and learning how to trade manually.

Do Binance Trading Bots Guarantee Profits?

No, Binance trading bots do not guarantee profits. While they can help traders earn profit, they automate trades based on predefined strategies. Therefore, the bot cannot be profitable if the trader’s strategy or instructions are flawed or the markets go against them.

title: Crypto News Today: Waller’s Rate-Hike Warning, MARA’s $1.1B Bitcoin Sale and USDC’s EU Deadline
summary: A fresh inflation reading tests Waller’s rate-hike warning as MARA discloses a $1.1 billion Bitcoin sale and USDC approaches an EU oversight milestone.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC MARA USDC

A fresh inflation reading tests Waller’s rate-hike warning as MARA discloses a $1.1 billion Bitcoin sale and USDC approaches an EU oversight milestone.

Crypto news today is being shaped by three different pressures on digital money: a Federal Reserve official keeping a half-point rate increase on the table, a major miner selling Bitcoin to repay loans, and Europe preparing to take a bigger supervisory role over USDC.

For November 11 in New Zealand, the freshest developments come from Tuesday’s U.S. inflation release and Monday’s MARA disclosure, alongside a November 12 regulatory handover. Together, they show why crypto investors need to watch the cost of money, the decisions of large holders and the rules governing stablecoins.

Bitcoin’s inflation test: Waller raises the stakes

U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4% in October after September’s 0.6% increase, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics release. Core CPI, excluding food and energy, increased 0.3% for a third consecutive month. Headline inflation slowed on a monthly basis, but the underlying measure did not.

That matters because Fed Governor Christopher Waller had drawn attention to precisely that kind of reading in a speech delivered before the figures were released. If October core CPI remained around 0.3% or higher, he said, a stronger policy response might be needed.

“I believe a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting,” Waller said.

The data therefore met the condition he had described. That is an important connection, but it is not a Fed decision or a post-release endorsement from Waller. His speech expressed his own views, and the committee still has to decide policy.

The distinction for Bitcoin is between inflation improving and improving enough to ease monetary pressure. Higher rates can make cash and interest-bearing assets more attractive, increasing the competition facing assets that produce no contractual yield.

There is also a data trap: BLS could not publish October annual changes for most CPI series because survey data was not collected in October 2025 during a funding lapse. Estimates circulating elsewhere should not be presented as an official headline annual rate.

BNC’s coverage of the inflation release and crypto-market response examines the immediate trading picture. The policy question is what persistent monthly price increases mean for December.

MARA discloses $1.1 billion Bitcoin sale

The second development comes from a company that creates Bitcoin rather than merely trades it. MARA disclosed that it sold 13,597 BTC after September 30 at an average of approximately $81,039, raising around $1.1 billion.

Its third-quarter shareholder letter, filed November 9, says $750 million was used to repay Bitcoin-collateralised term loans, releasing 17,477 pledged coins. MARA had reported 34,012 BTC at quarter-end; the subsequent sales equalled roughly 40% of that amount, a scale comparison rather than a calculation of its current holdings.

“We expect to continue to monetize bitcoin to enhance our financial flexibility,” the company wrote. It said proceeds could provide liquidity or finance capital projects and other initiatives, subject to conditions and allocation priorities.

The disclosure challenges the assumption that a corporate Bitcoin balance is a permanent withdrawal of coins from the market. For an operating company, those coins can also be a financing resource.

Repaying collateralised borrowing can reduce financial exposure even as selling reduces Bitcoin holdings. Those are separate effects. A large sale is therefore not automatically evidence that management expects the asset to fall; investors need to examine the use of proceeds.

Nor should the newly disclosed total be mistaken for a single trade executed today. The sales took place after quarter-end. The fresh information is their disclosure and the explanation of how management is using the balance sheet.

USDC faces an EU supervision change on November 12

While Bitcoin investors assess rates and corporate selling, stablecoin users face a different milestone. USDC issued by Circle Internet Financial Europe SAS is due to enter dual supervision on November 12 under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets framework, or MiCA.

The European Banking Authority announced the classification on October 14, making USDC the first significant e-money token under the framework. The approaching implementation date gives that earlier decision its immediate relevance.

The EBA will assume direct responsibilities for own funds, reserves, liquidity requirements, and recovery and redemption plans. France’s ACPR will retain oversight of areas including governance, outsourcing and conflicts of interest. This is shared supervision, rather than the French regulator disappearing from the picture.

For users and businesses, the practical issue is who oversees the resources and processes supporting redemption. The announcement does not establish a new return for holders or promise a trading gain. It makes oversight of a widely used payment and settlement instrument more concrete.

What to watch next in crypto

These stories point to three separate tests. Will further Fed communications reinforce Waller’s tightening argument? Will subsequent corporate disclosures show continued Bitcoin sales and explain their purpose? And does USDC’s supervisory handover proceed on the announced timetable?

A rebound in token prices would not settle those questions. The useful signals are changes in policy expectations, actual capital allocation and the operation of redemption safeguards. Those developments will help distinguish a short-lived market bounce from an improvement in the conditions supporting crypto demand.

title: US Inflation Data Shakes Crypto Market as Bitcoin Breaks Below $73K Support
summary: Bitcoin broke below the $73,000 support level on November 10 after hotter-than-expected US inflation data strengthened expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate increase in December.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC ETH XRP

Bitcoin broke below the $73,000 support level on November 10 after hotter-than-expected US inflation data strengthened expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate increase in December.

The decline intensified selling pressure across the cryptocurrency market, with Ethereum, XRP, and Solana also posting substantial losses as Bitcoin extended its slide.

The October Consumer Price Index (CPI) increased 0.4% month over month, exceeding the 0.3% forecast, while core inflation rose 0.3% against expectations of 0.2%. The latest figures reinforced concerns about persistent inflation and reduced expectations of monetary easing.

October US CPI Exceeds Market Expectations

The US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported that headline CPI increased 0.4% in October, following a 0.6% advance in September. Although the monthly increase slowed, it remained above economists’ expectations, indicating that inflationary pressures had not eased as quickly as markets anticipated.

Headline inflation rose 0.4% MoM and core CPI 0.3%, both exceeding forecasts and signaling persistent price pressures following September’s 0.6% increase. Source: Crypto Rover via X

Core CPI, which excludes food and energy prices, also exceeded forecasts. The index increased 0.3% during the month, compared with the expected 0.2%. Notably, core inflation maintained the same monthly growth rate for a third consecutive month, following similar increases in August and September.

Several spending categories contributed to the latest increase. Shelter costs advanced 0.3% in October, accounting for more than 30% of the monthly rise in overall consumer prices. Food prices increased 0.5%, while energy costs climbed 0.7% following a much sharper 5.2% increase in September.

The October report also came with an important data limitation. The BLS did not publish year-over-year inflation figures because the 2025 government shutdown prevented the collection of October 2025 price data, leaving no comparable base for calculating the annual change.

Consequently, investors had to assess the latest inflation trend primarily through monthly figures. The absence of an annual reading added another layer of uncertainty to an already sensitive economic outlook.

Bitcoin Price Breaks Below $73K Support After CPI Release

Bitcoin faced renewed selling pressure shortly after the inflation figures became public. The cryptocurrency was trading near $74,264 before the November 10 CPI announcement but quickly declined to approximately $73,494 within five minutes of the release.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Selling continued during the session, eventually pushing BTC below the closely watched $73,000 support level. Investing.com market data showed Bitcoin reaching an intraday low of approximately $72,836 before recovering to around $73,294 in its later market snapshot at 11:01 a.m. ET.

The latest move marks a further deterioration in Bitcoin’s short-term price structure. Although BTC recovered above $73,000 after briefly breaking below it, the level remains an important area for traders monitoring whether buyers can regain control.

The decline also extended an existing period of weakness rather than marking an entirely new downturn. Bitcoin had already struggled to regain $75,000 as investors monitored tightening monetary policy expectations and withdrawals from US spot Bitcoin ETFs.

Those investment products recorded approximately $201 million in net outflows on November 9, marking their third consecutive session of withdrawals. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounted for $213.2 million in redemptions, although inflows into other Bitcoin funds partially offset the withdrawals. Total net outflows across the Bitcoin ETF category remained near $201 million.

The combination of weaker institutional flows and uncertainty surrounding Federal Reserve policy added to the pressure on Bitcoin. The latest CPI reading introduced another obstacle for buyers attempting to stabilize the market above recent support levels.

Federal Reserve Rate Hike Expectations Put Pressure on Crypto

The inflation report strengthened expectations that the Federal Reserve could continue tightening monetary policy at its December 8–9 meeting. Higher interest rates generally create less favorable conditions for speculative investments, including cryptocurrencies, as investors reassess the relative appeal of cash and fixed-income assets.

The latest reading also aligned with concerns raised by Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller before the CPI announcement. Waller indicated that he would support a 25-basis-point rate increase in December even if inflation showed signs of cooling.

However, he also warned that a stronger policy response could become necessary if underlying price pressures remained elevated.

“If core consumer prices rise 0.3% or more from September, ‘a stronger policy move may be needed,'” Waller said, adding that a 50-basis-point increase should be considered.

October’s core CPI subsequently reached that 0.3% threshold, reinforcing the discussion around a potentially larger increase. Reuters reported that market expectations for a 50-basis-point increase climbed to nearly 15% by midmorning, while a quarter-point hike was already considered almost certain.

The combination of stronger employment and persistent inflation presents a difficult policy environment. The Federal Reserve must balance its inflation target against the risk of weakening economic activity through additional rate increases.

For cryptocurrency investors, the possibility of higher borrowing costs for longer could limit expectations of near-term monetary easing. A stronger dollar and rising Treasury yields also tend to reduce demand for risk-sensitive assets.

Crypto Liquidations Exceed $170M After Inflation Report

The sharp Bitcoin decline triggered another wave of forced closures across leveraged cryptocurrency positions. Within an hour of the October CPI announcement, approximately $178 million in crypto long positions were liquidated, according to liquidation data reported by TokenPost.

More than $170 million in long positions were liquidated within minutes as Bitcoin fell below $74,000 and Ethereum dropped under $2,050, hitting 11-week lows amid heavy leverage. Source: @BullTheoryio via X

Long positions represent leveraged bets that an asset’s price will increase. When prices move against traders, exchanges can automatically close positions after their collateral falls below required maintenance levels. These forced closures can accelerate selling during periods of heightened volatility.

The latest liquidation activity followed an already significant wave of leveraged position closures. CoinDesk reported that cryptocurrency futures liquidations had reached approximately $1.1 billion during the preceding 24-hour period on November 9, with long positions accounting for most of the total.

That earlier figure reflected the broader market decline before the November 10 CPI announcement and should not be attributed entirely to the inflation release. Nevertheless, it showed that leveraged traders were already facing substantial losses as Bitcoin traded around the $72,800–$75,000 range.

The additional liquidations following the CPI publication demonstrated how quickly unexpected economic data can affect leveraged cryptocurrency markets. With traders positioned for a recovery, the sudden decline forced further exits and added to downward price pressure.

Ethereum and XRP Extend Crypto Market Losses

The selling pressure also extended to other digital assets. Ethereum traded near $2,027 after falling below the $2,100 level and touching an intraday low of approximately $2,006. The asset was down around 4.54% over 24 hours in the latest Investing.com market snapshot.

Ethereum (ETH) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

XRP also extended its decline, trading near $1.05 after reaching approximately $1.0336. Its 24-hour loss stood near 3.69%, placing the token under additional pressure after several consecutive sessions of weakness.

Solana recorded a similar downturn, trading around $82.49 after touching an intraday low of approximately $81.59. The token declined roughly 5.2% over the preceding 24 hours.

The simultaneous declines across Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, and Solana reflected broader weakness in cryptocurrency markets rather than an isolated move in BTC.

XRP price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Ethereum and XRP also entered the session following several days of negative price action. Their latest losses highlighted the sensitivity of digital assets to changing expectations around US monetary policy and broader financial market conditions.

Bitcoin’s break below $73,000 has brought the next support areas into focus. BRN analysts previously identified $73,000 as an important level, warning that a daily close below it could expose BTC to a decline toward $70,000. Bitget Wallet analysts also highlighted the $73,000–$74,000 region as an important support zone, with a deeper breakdown potentially exposing $68,000.

For now, Bitcoin’s ability to reclaim and maintain the $73,000 level remains important for assessing short-term market direction. The December Federal Reserve meeting, upcoming inflation readings, and changes in institutional investment flows are likely to remain key factors influencing cryptocurrency prices.

title: Canaan (CAN) Swings to an $8 Million Profit on Bitcoin Gains as Rig Sales Collapse 96%
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Canaan (CAN) Swings to an $8 Million Profit on Bitcoin Gains as Rig Sales Collapse 96%
Canaan's mining-machine sales fell to $4.8 million from $118.6 million a year earlier, but a $51.9 million fair-value gain turned an operating loss into $8.0 million of net income.
This post Cana...
content:
Canaan Inc. (NASDAQ: CAN) swung to $8.0 million of third-quarter net income on a $51.9 million fair-value gain in its bitcoin holdings and derivatives, the mining-rig maker said Tuesday, even as machine sales collapsed 96%.

The company filed the unaudited results Tuesday in a 6-K with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Total revenue fell to $14.5 million from $150.5 million a year earlier, including $4.8 million from product sales and $9.5 million from mining. Canaan sold 1.0 million terahashes per second of computing power and mined 133 bitcoin.

The profit did not come from the business. Canaan posted an $8.6 million gross loss and a $42.9 million operating loss. Chief financial officer Jin “James” Cheng said a recovery in bitcoin prices toward quarter-end generated the $51.9 million fair-value gain and called it “distinct from underlying operating performance.”

The $51.9 million is the sum of a $20.1 million gain on cryptocurrency and a $31.9 million gain on financial derivatives. Canaan also reported $22.4 million of non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA, a figure that still includes those gains. Strip them out and adjusted EBITDA would have been a loss of about $29.5 million.

Nangeng Zhang, Canaan’s chairman and chief executive officer, pointed to “continued weakness in bitcoin mining equipment demand and intense industry pricing competition.” Products revenue dropped from $13.6 million in the second quarter and from $118.6 million in the same period of 2025. The company blamed lower volumes and a lower average selling price.

The treasury carries the quarter

Canaan took $8.2 million of inventory-related write-downs, down from $25.3 million in the second quarter. Mining operations posted a gross margin of about 30% before depreciation, with an all-in power cost of about $0.043 per kilowatt-hour and roughly 10 exahashes per second of installed capacity outside joint ventures.

The company held 1,875.5 bitcoin as of Sept. 30. Of that, 517.5 coins were owned outright, 1,258 were pledged for secured term loans and 100 sat in a fixed-term product. It booked $43.7 million of cryptocurrency assets and $114.2 million of cryptocurrency receivables.

The stack is down about 40 bitcoin from the 1,915.5 Canaan reported at the end of the second quarter, even after the company mined 133 in the period, implying it moved roughly 173 bitcoin off the treasury. Zhang said Canaan is “selectively monetizing cryptocurrency holdings to fund share repurchases.”

On Nov. 6, the board approved a new $100 million share repurchase authorization over 12 months and launched an initial $20 million program under that cap.

A 2-gigawatt Texas bet, and a reverse split

Canaan is trying to recast itself around power and compute infrastructure. Its 1-gigawatt project in Duval County, Texas, received a conditional “Studied Load – Firm” classification under ERCOT’s Batch Zero process, a grid-connection step Zhang said remains “subject to further studies and approvals.” A second 1-gigawatt project in Zapata County is in early-stage development.

To support those plans, Canaan set aside $50 million of restricted cash as collateral for a letter of credit tied to infrastructure contracts and made about $3.3 million of project prepayments. In October it bought a parcel of U.S. land for about $1.1 million. Cash ended Sept. 30 at $72.8 million, $50 million of it restricted, leaving $22.8 million unrestricted.

Canaan also plans a 1-for-25 reverse ADS split, effective on or about Dec. 4, changing each ADS from 15 Class A ordinary shares to 375. The move is meant to help the company regain compliance with Nasdaq’s minimum bid price requirement.

For the fourth quarter, Canaan expects revenue of $18 million to $22 million.

The shift toward power and compute puts Canaan in the same lane as other public bitcoin miners. MARA sold 13,597 bitcoin to fund AI infrastructure, and Hyperscale Data sold its last coins for a Michigan data center.

Whether a paper gain on 1,875 bitcoin and a pair of early-stage Texas power projects can carry Canaan until customers start buying machines again is the question the quarter leaves open.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Binance Warns iOS Flaw Could Expose Wallet Seed Phrases as Apple’s Latest iPhone Patch Stays Silent
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Binance Warns iOS Flaw Could Expose Wallet Seed Phrases as Apple’s Latest iPhone Patch Stays Silent
Binance told iPhone users a public iOS sandbox escape called worse_query could let malicious apps read seed phrases and private keys stored by other apps, while Apple's Nov. 9 update...
content:
Binance warned iPhone users Tuesday that a publicly released iOS flaw could let malicious apps read files stored by other apps, including the seed phrases and private keys that control crypto wallets.

“A vulnerability (worse_query) affecting iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 allows malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem,” the exchange wrote on X. “This is an iOS-level issue, not unique to Binance.”

Binance told users to delete any apps installed from untrusted sources, such as sideloaded or manually signed IPA files, and to update iOS and every app to the latest official versions. Anyone who suspects a breach should move funds to a new wallet created on a clean device and reset all active login sessions, the exchange said.

Neither Binance nor the researcher behind the flaw has reported any thefts tied to it.

What worse_query does

The bug is a sandbox escape. On iOS, each app is supposed to live in its own container that other apps cannot read. A researcher who posts as forcequitOS released worse_query on GitHub on Nov. 8, calling it “a zero-day sandbox escape for iOS 26 and 27, again.” It succeeds an earlier exploit, bad_query.

The project’s README says it works on iOS 26.0 through 26.7.2 and on iOS 27.2, a wider range than the versions Binance named. It lists paths it can reach, including other apps’ data containers and shared app group folders.

The researcher describes it as “a proof-of-concept for developers” that “isn’t useful by itself,” and stresses it is not a jailbreak. To use it, a developer has to build it into an app.

That has already happened in at least one case. A day after the release, developer Christoph Kolbicz published a file manager built on worse_query that lets users browse and edit app data on iOS 27 without jailbreaking, which he said was tested on iOS 27.0.1.

Blockchain security firm SlowMist called worse_query a container sandbox escape rather than a jailbreak. Its chief information security officer, who posts as 23pds, wrote that the flaw will not steal assets on its own. The risk comes when a user installs and runs an untrusted IPA that then reads other apps’ containers, and only if a wallet stores mnemonic phrases, keystores or WebView caches in plain text on the device.

Apple’s iOS updates don’t mention it

Apple shipped iOS 27.2.1 and iOS 26.7.3 on Nov. 9, a day after the proof of concept went public. Their security notes list fixes for AirPlay, Bluetooth pairing, brotli and other components, but neither names worse_query or describes a sandbox escape of this kind.

That leaves it unclear whether the latest iOS builds block the technique.

The exposure depends heavily on how each wallet app stores secrets. By SlowMist’s reading, wallets that do not write recovery phrases or keys to plain files on the device are not exposed in the same way, and hardware wallets keep private keys off the phone entirely. The attack also requires a user to install software from outside the App Store first.

The warning comes from an exchange still recovering from its own breach. Binance lost $6.34 billion in an Oct. 29 attack that began with a fake job interview. Security worries have also pushed some large holders to swap self-custodied bitcoin for IBIT shares, while hardware wallet maker Ledger said an organized crime group spent millions targeting its users.

For iPhone users holding bitcoin in a mobile wallet, Binance’s advice amounts to basic hygiene: stay on official iOS releases, skip sideloaded apps and move funds if a device may have been compromised.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

content:
Binance Launchpad is a platform by Binance for launching new cryptocurrency tokens. It enables early-stage blockchain projects to raise funds and gain exposure by launching their native tokens. Binance reviews each project before listing it to ensure it is safe and legitimate.

To take part in a Binance Launchpad token sale, you must verify your Binance account, hold some BNB in your wallet, visit the Launchpad page during an active sale, lock your BNB during the subscription time, and then the exchange will distribute the token allocation.

In this guide, we will explain what Binance Launchpad is, how it works, and its advantages and drawbacks. We will also list the steps to join Binance Launchpad token sales and show you the top Binance Launchpad projects by market capitalization.
