Binance Launchpad Review? What is It?

Binance Launchpad is a platform on the Binance cryptocurrency exchange that enables new blockchain projects to raise funds by selling their native tokens to Binance users, a process known as an Initial Exchange Offering (IEO). Here, Binance carefully vets each project before listing it on the Launchpad, thereby adding a layer of credibility for investors.

You must hold a certain amount of Binance coin (BNB) or FDUSD stablecoin in your account to participate in these token sales and then subscribe to the sale during the subscription period. It’s an opportunity for you to invest early in projects that have the potential to take off. Usually, they use a fair system, such as a lottery or subscription, to ensure everyone has a decent chance at the tokens. Generally, having more BNB means having more tickets and a higher chance of obtaining the tokens.

Later, all new tokens are listed on Binance after the sale ends, enabling immediate trading without reliance on external exchanges. Today, Binance Launchpad is recognized for supporting prominent projects such as Axie Infinity, Sandbox, and Injective.

How Does Binance Launchpad Work?

Binance Launchpad serves as a token sale platform, helping new crypto projects launch, raise funds, and reach a global audience. First, a new project that wants to launch its crypto tokens on Binance Launchpad must be very authentic, as Binance thoroughly checks these projects to ensure they are strong and have a genuine purpose.

Now, Binance announces the project on the Launchpad after it has been chosen, and then, people who use Binance and hold a certain amount of Binance Coin (BNB) can sign up to support the new project. Often, a lottery system is in place, meaning not everyone who signs up will be able to purchase the new tokens. The more BNB you have, the more chances you get in this lottery.

In the lottery system, BNB holders receive tickets. Then, Binance randomly selects winning tickets. And hence, only winners can buy the new tokens. After the sale, Binance lists the token on its exchange. You can easily trade or sell your allocation directly.

How to Launch a Project on Binance Launchpad?

To launch a project on Binance Launchpad, you need to meet its requirements, submit an application, undergo review, gain approval, and successfully list your project.

  1. Meet Binance’s Criteria: Your project must be well-structured and thoughtfully designed. Binance is seeking talented teams, innovative crypto projects, and a vibrant community. They want to see that your project can make a positive impact in the world of cryptocurrency.
  2. Submit Your Application: You must complete an application form on the Binance website. The form requests a significant amount of information about your project, including your business idea, the operation of your token, and details about your team. Ensure you get everything right and fill it out correctly.
  3. Undergo Review: Binance will thoroughly review your project once you apply. They will examine your plans, the level of development your project has reached, and whether it has the potential for expansion. This process may take time.
  4. Get Approved and Get Ready: Once they review your project, Binance will approve it for Launchpad. You’ll then collaborate with Binance to arrange the token sale. This means determining the specifics, such as the number of tokens to sell and the price at which to sell them.
  5. Launch and List: When everything is set, your token sale will go live on Binance Launchpad. After the sale concludes, Binance typically lists your tokens on its main exchange, and users can trade them.

What Are the Advantages of Binance Launchpad?

The advantages of Binance Launchpad include its large audience and exposure, robust trust and safety measures, early investment opportunities for users, and strong support provided to projects.

  • Big Audience and Exposure: Projects launched here are exposed to millions of Binance users globally. This means that a significant number of potential investors are immediately exposed to the project. It makes new projects well-known instantly.
  • Trust and Safety: Binance thoroughly vets every project before it appears on Launchpad. Hence, this reduces the risk of scams or poor projects, making investors feel more secure.
  • Early Investment Opportunities: Investors have the opportunity to purchase new tokens at a special, usually discounted, price. With the success of the project, early investments can be very profitable.
  • Solid Backing for Projects: Binance not only lists projects but also offers guidance and marketing support. Having this kind of backing from such a large platform can significantly improve a new project’s potential for success. Generally, they deliver useful resources in addition to fundraising.

What Are the Potential Drawbacks of Binance Launchpad?

The drawbacks of Binance Launchpad are the high demand and limited allocation for participants, the requirement to hold BNB, the inherent market volatility of newly launched tokens, and the locking up of your funds during the sale period.

  • High Demand and Limited Allocation: A lot of individuals wish to participate in Launchpad sales, so it is usually extremely competitive. This indicates that even when you join in, you may only receive a small portion of the new tokens. You may find it challenging to secure a large share.
  • Requirement to Hold BNB: To participate, you generally must hold a decent amount of Binance Coin (BNB). The more BNB you hold, the higher your chances of receiving a better allocation. This can be a disadvantage for users who don’t want to hold BNB.
  • Market Volatility: Prices of newly-listed tokens can fluctuate rapidly. Although there is potential for large gains, there is also the possibility that prices may fall after listing. Keep in mind that crypto markets are volatile.
  • Locking Up Funds: When you commit BNB in a Launchpad sale, your funds will be locked for a short time. Your BNB will not be available for use in other trading activities during this period.

How to Buy Binance Launchpad Token Sales?

To join a Binance Launchpad token sale, you need to have a verified Binance account, hold Binance Coin (BNB), go to the Launchpad page when a sale is active, commit your BNB during the subscription period, and then receive your allocated tokens.

Step 1: Have a Verified Binance Account

First, you must have an account on Binance. Your account must be fully verified through the Know Your Customer (KYC) process. This check is necessary for you to participate in these sales. So, go to the “Identification” section and complete KYC.

Step 2: Hold Binance Coin (BNB) or FDUSD

Most Launchpad sales need you to hold a certain amount of BNB or FDUSD tokens in your Binance wallet. As discussed above, the more BNB you have, the more chances or a bigger share you might get in the sale. Generally, Binance will take snapshots of your BNB holdings over a few days before the sale.

Step 3: Go to the Launchpad Page

Now, when a new project is announced, go to the Binance website or app and find the “Launchpool” section. Here, you will see details about the upcoming token sale, like the project’s information and the timeline for the sale. Mainly, you should look for the “Subscription Period” start date.

Step 4: Commit Your BNB During Subscription

As the Subscription Period opens, you need to go to the specific project’s Launchpad page and “commit” your BNB. Here, you must agree to use a certain amount of your BNB to buy the new tokens, and now, your BNB will be locked during this short period.

Step 5: Receive Your Tokens

After the BNB commitment period ends, Binance will calculate how many new tokens you get based on your committed BNB and the total BNB committed by all participants. Your allocated new tokens will be sent to your Spot Wallet, and any unused BNB will be returned to you instantly.

Rules and Restrictions for Participation

The rules for joining Binance Launchpad include complete KYC, checking if your country is allowed, holding BNB, committing BNB during the specific period, and understanding that there are per-user limits and market risks.

  • Identity Verification (KYC): You must finish your identity check on Binance. Go and provide your personal ID details and documents so Binance knows who you are. Without this, you cannot join.
  • Geographical Restrictions: Not everyone from every country can join, as Binance has rules about which countries are allowed to participate in Launchpad sales. In this stage, regulatory restrictions may apply, so verify your country’s eligibility.
  • BNB Holding Requirement: For most sales, you need to hold Binance Coin (BNB) in your account. The amount of BNB you hold over a certain period will decide how many new tokens you might get.
  • Commitment During Subscription: You can only “commit” your BNB during a specific time window, called the subscription period. And if you miss this time, you cannot join that sale. Hence, be sure to mark your calendar.
  • Per-User Caps: There is often a limit on how many tokens each person can get. This is to make sure many people have a chance to buy, not just a few big investors. You might not get all the tokens you want.
  • No Market Orders: When committing BNB, you usually cannot use market orders or instant buys. You must commit your BNB during the subscription window, specifically for the Launchpad sale.

Top Binance Launchpad Projects by Market Capitalization

The top Binance Launchpad projects by market capitalization include POL (Polygon), FET (Fetch.ai), INJ (Injective), SAND (The Sandbox), AXS (Axie Infinity Shards), BTTC (BitTorrent-New), EGLD (MultiversX), KAVA (Kava), ARKM (Arkham), and SFP (SafePal).

1. POL

Polygon, which was known as Matic Network before, is a scaling solution for Ethereum. Mainly, it helps to make transactions on Ethereum much faster and cheaper, and this is done by acting like a second layer, a “Layer 2” solution. 

Polygon lets different blockchains connect and work together, building what some call an “Internet of Blockchains”. The POL token is used for paying small fees, staking to keep the network safe, and helping to vote on project changes. The token is also available for futures trading on Binance. If you want to trade leverage, here is our Binance futures review for you.

2. FET

Fetch.ai is a project that brings together smart computer programs, called artificial intelligence (AI), with blockchain technology. Here, the main goal is to make a world where AI programs can find each other and share information. 

Fetch.ai automates tasks like financial trading and energy grid optimization. The FET token is used for payments and for building these AI programs on the Fetch.ai network.

3. INJ

Injective is a blockchain that is made just for finance. It helps people build decentralized trading platforms. Now, these platforms can be for many things, like regular buying and selling, or more complex financial products. 

The main idea is to have very fast and secure trading without a central company controlling everything. The INJ token is used to pay network fees and for people to vote on how the network should change and update over time.

4. SAND

The Sandbox is a metaverse world that you can explore. In this world, players can make their own games, digital items, and art, and these creations are exclusively owned by the players themselves, using blockchain technology, specifically as NFTs. 

People can then sell these items in the game’s marketplace. SAND is the main token used for all things in The Sandbox, like buying land or trading items.

5. AXS

Axie Infinity is a game where people collect small, unique digital creatures called Axies. Also, players can make new Axies, fight battles with them, and trade them with others. 

This game allows players to earn money by playing, which is called “play-to-earn”. AXS is the governance token that gives players a say in how the game is run. Holders can vote on important decisions about the game’s future.

6. BTTC

BitTorrent-New is a new version of the very old BitTorrent file-sharing system. The new version leverages blockchain to enhance file-sharing efficiency and security. 

The BTTC token is used for different things on the network, like rewarding people who share files or speeding up downloads.

7. EGLD

MultiversX was formerly called Elrond. It is a blockchain that can handle many transactions very fast, as it uses a method called “adaptive state sharding” to divide the work, allowing it to process thousands of transactions each second. 

This makes it a very scalable blockchain. Here, EGLD is the main token for this network, and it is used for transaction fees, securing the network by staking, and also for voting on network changes.

8. KAVA

Kava is a platform for decentralized finance, or “DeFi”. It lets people do things like borrow and lend cryptocurrency. 

It is best because it combines the power of Ethereum and Cosmos blockchains. And hence, this helps Kava to be very fast and also to work with many different crypto assets. KAVA is the token used to secure the network and also to take part in making decisions for the platform.

9. ARKM

Arkham is a blockchain intelligence tool. It helps you track and analyze on-chain data. It uses AI-powered tools to deanonymize blockchain addresses and link them to real-world entities like exchanges, firms, or individuals.

The platform also has an “Intel Exchange” where people can buy and sell information about crypto addresses. ARKM is the token for this platform, used to access its services.

10. SFP

SafePal makes secure wallets for crypto storage. They make both physical wallets that look like a small device, and software wallets for phones. Today, these wallets help people keep their crypto assets safe and easy to manage. 

SafePal was the very first hardware wallet project that Binance Labs invested in. SFP is the token for SafePal. It can be used for discounts on products, earning rewards, and voting on new features for the wallet.

Is Binance Launchpad Safe and Profitable?

Yes, Binance Launchpad has a good level of safety. Binance checks each project very carefully before it is listed on the Launchpad. They look at the project team, their idea, and whether it is real. This helps reduce the chance of scams. You can also read our Binance review to know more about the exchange.

About being profitable, many projects launched on Binance Launchpad have indeed seen their value go up a lot after they were first offered. This means some early investors have made good profits. However, this is not guaranteed for every project. The crypto market can change very fast. Also, many people want to join these sales, so it is often hard to get a big share of the new tokens. So, there is potential for profit, but there are also risks, and success is not certain.

Can You Make Money With Binance Launchpad?

Yes, you can make money with Binance Launchpad. Many projects launched there have done very well in the past, and you can get new crypto tokens at a very low price before they are traded publicly. 

So, if the project becomes popular, the price of these tokens can go up a lot after they are listed on the main exchange. This is how people can make a profit. But as discussed above, this is not certain. There are risks, and you should do your research carefully. title: Miami-Dade County Now Accepts Bitcoin for Property Taxes
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Miami-Dade County Now Accepts Bitcoin for Property Taxes
Miami-Dade Tax Collector Dariel Fernandez said Monday his office now accepts bitcoin for property taxes online and in person, with every payment converted to dollars before it reaches the county.
This post Miami-Dade County N...
content:
Miami-Dade County Tax Collector Dariel Fernandez said Monday his office has begun accepting bitcoin for property tax payments, both online and in person, while converting every transaction into dollars before the money reaches the county.

Fernandez announced the change in a statement on the Tax Collector’s website, calling it a way to give property owners another option without putting public funds into the asset. Payers can select a cryptocurrency option during online checkout or request it at the counter, then connect a supported exchange account or digital wallet and authorize the payment.

A third-party system converts the bitcoin into U.S. dollars at the time of payment, the office said, so it never holds, invests in or manages any cryptocurrency. The office said it still receives the full dollar amount owed and records the transactions in its standard payment reports, without county workers maintaining digital wallets.

“Government must keep up with the times and the needs of the people we serve,” Fernandez said. “By accepting Bitcoin as a payment option, we are giving property owners another way to pay their taxes, whether online or in person, while continuing to offer the traditional payment methods they already know and trust.”

He added that the office is “embracing new technology without compromising our responsibility to protect taxpayer dollars.” Whether someone pays with bitcoin or a conventional method, he said, “our office receives the full amount owed in U.S. dollars.”

The office did not name the payment processor or say whether bitcoin payments carry a convenience fee. Card and mobile-wallet payments already carry a nonrefundable 2.50% fee online, with a $2.50 minimum, the office’s payment-methods page shows. Traditional options, including checks, cards, cash and fee-free eChecks, remain available. The announcement covers property taxes, and the option is voluntary.

A 4% discount is still on the clock

The change landed in the middle of Florida’s property tax collection season. Miami-Dade opened the 2026 tax roll on Oct. 30 and is urging owners to pay by Nov. 30 to lock in a 4% early-payment discount under Florida law. The discount falls to 3% in December, 2% in January and 1% in February, with the full amount due in March. Unpaid bills generally become delinquent April 1.

Under the office’s existing rules, discounts are based on the date a payment is submitted online or in person. Fernandez has been promoting a “Save the Max” campaign around that calendar, noting that an eligible $5,000 tax bill would save $200 if paid in November. Payments can be made at the office’s 13 locations, through T-Connect mobile units or online around the clock at mdctaxcollector.gov.

Miami’s long courtship of bitcoin payments

The move closes a loop the county opened years ago. In 2021, Miami-Dade Commissioner Danielle Cohen Higgins put forward a resolution to study letting residents pay county taxes and fees with bitcoin, after Miami Mayor Francis Suarez pushed to let residents pay city fees and taxes in bitcoin and explored paying city workers in it. The city of Miami also launched MiamiCoin, a token tied to the Stacks protocol, as part of that campaign.

Fernandez, elected in November 2024, had earlier served on Miami-Dade’s Cryptocurrency Task Force, his official biography notes.

The office called Miami-Dade one of the first government agencies in the country to accept the payments. Colorado has taken cryptocurrency for state taxes since 2022, converting it to dollars through a third party, and Utah later opened a similar option for individual income taxes. Detroit announced in 2024 that it would start accepting cryptocurrency for city taxes and fees in mid-2025, also settling in dollars.

Florida lawmakers, meanwhile, revived a 2026 bill to create a state Strategic Cryptocurrency Reserve after a 2025 effort was withdrawn. The Senate measure, CS/SB 1038, died in an appropriations committee in March and never became law.

For now, Miami-Dade is offering a narrower door: bitcoin can be used to pay the property tax bill, and the county keeps none of it.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Binance Flags iOS Flaw That Could Expose iPhone Users’ Crypto Wallets and Private Keys
summary:
Key Takeaways: Binance warns users that iOS has a vulnerability called ‘worse_query’ that might leave other apps’ files exposed. Owned devices could possibly be vulnerable to losing seed phrases, private
The post Binance Flags iOS Flaw That Could Expose iPhone Users’ Crypto Wallets and Private Keys ...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Binance warns users that iOS has a vulnerability called ‘worse_query’ that might leave other apps’ files exposed.
  • Owned devices could possibly be vulnerable to losing seed phrases, private keys, and logins.
  • Users should remove apps that they believe are untrusted, update their software, and withdraw any funds to a new wallet if they suspect a breach.

A security flaw in Apple’s iOS operating system could potentially lead to the leakage of sensitive data from apps, including cryptocurrency wallets, according to Binance. The exchange states the problem is called “worse_query”, and it occurs across several different iOS versions and may enable malicious applications to access local files belonging to other apps.

A vulnerability (worse_query) affecting iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 allows malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem. This is an iOS-level issue, not unique to Binance.

Immediate Action Required:
– Delete any apps installed from untrusted sources (such as sideloaded or manually signed IPAs).
– Update iOS and all apps to the latest official versions.
– If you suspect a breach, transfer funds to a new wallet created on a clean device and reset all active login sessions.

Never install unauthorized packages, and keep your software up to date.

— Binance (@binance) November 10, 2026

  • Binance Identifies Risk to Crypto Wallet Security
  • Binance Recommends Immediate Security Measures
    • What Crypto Holders Should Do if a Breach Is Suspected

Binance Identifies Risk to Crypto Wallet Security

Binance has warned that the flaw applies to iOS versions 26.7.1, 27.0.1 and 27.2. It could also enable a malicious application to access locally stored data from other servers, thus exposing information that users might want to keep confidential.

The concern for the crypto owners is that wallet apps can be done or consist of watching to delicate credentials. That includes seed phrases, private keys, and some type of account log in info. Attackers who get a hold of this can possibly control the digital assets of a user.

Binance said this is not a Binance login vulnerability, but a problem in Apple’s operating system. Thus, if they are impacted, users employing different kinds of cryptocurrency applications might be subjected to similar dangers.

Read More: Binance Reveals How Hackers Moved $6.34B After Breaching Its Wallet-Signing System

Binance Recommends Immediate Security Measures

The exchange recommended that users of iPhones screen the apps installed and delete any others they are not familiar with. That means applications that have been sideloaded or manually signed IPA packages, especially if they are not clear of their origin.

Users should also ensure that both iOS and apps are on the latest official versions that are available. Binance’s caution is not intended to prove that all impacted devices have been hacked, but it likely means that keeping software current can minimize vulnerabilities to known attacks that are posing a risk.

What Crypto Holders Should Do if a Breach Is Suspected

Binance advises those who feel their devices might have been infected to move their balances over to a fresh wallet that has been built on a clean gadget. They should also have the capability to terminate or invalidate active logon sessions to minimize the potential of unauthorized logon.

The exchange also warned its users of the danger of installing non-authorized software packages that could pose extra threats to security.

The warning highlights the importance of protecting wallet credentials beyond the security of cryptocurrency exchanges themselves. No matter how funds are stored, compromised devices can reveal the data that is required to access them.

Binance has not identified any confirmed cryptocurrency theft cases, though due to vulnerability. Instead, its advisory encourages users to take preventive action, as the iOS-level security concern continues.

title: Coinbase Wins Federal Trust Charter, Launching National Trust Company
summary:
Key Takeaways: The OCC granted Coinbase final approval to form Coinbase National Trust Company. The federal charter confers on a uniform framework that allows the exchange to further its digital
The post Coinbase Wins Federal Trust Charter, Launching National Trust Company appeared first on CryptoNi...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • The OCC granted Coinbase final approval to form Coinbase National Trust Company.
  • The federal charter confers on a uniform framework that allows the exchange to further its digital asset custody activities.
  • With over 14 years of holding crypto assets under custody, Coinbase is set to start with its fundamental custody services.

Now, Coinbase has gotten the final regulatory nod from the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to approve the nation’s trust company. The approval is for the exchange to continue to grow the portion of its activity it is regulated for by the federal government as an institution charging custody fees to hold securities.

  • Coinbase Secures OCC Approval for National Trust Company
  • A Federal Framework Builds on Existing State Oversight
    • Institutional Custody Is the Initial Focus

Coinbase Secures OCC Approval for National Trust Company

Coinbase announced that the OCC approved the charter for Coinbase National Trust Company (CNTC) on Friday, November 6. The company said that the move represents a fresh page in its history as a custody provider for institutional and other customers for over 10 years.

Introducing Coinbase National Trust Company, our federally chartered trust company.

OCC approved. https://t.co/jhqyDdFyLk

— Coinbase 🛡️ (@coinbase) November 9, 2026

The federal charter will offer a more uniform regulatory structure for Coinbase’s trust work. As digital assets increasingly link up with the traditional financial sector, the company will be better equipped to supervise its custody activities, it said.

Security and compliance and regulatory supervision are at the heart of Coinbase’s custody business. Additionally, it noted that support from key financial institutions is aiding it in its rise in the global crypto custody sector.

Read More: Coinbase Launches AI Agent Sign-Ups for Crypto Trading with Built-In Safety Limits

A Federal Framework Builds on Existing State Oversight

The approval comes on the heels of Coinbase’s previous regulatory ties with New York officials. The company received a BitLicense from the New York Department of Financial Services (NYDFS) in 2017. In 2018, Coinbase Custody Trust Company then applied for a New York chartered New Purpose Trust Company.

Another step in this federal regulatory approach is CNTC’s federal charter. Coinbase noted that they will run consistent and nationalized trust operations across Coinbase and build on their experience as a NYDFS trust.

Institutional Custody Is the Initial Focus

The new entity will start on its most core operation, the custody of digital assets, Coinbase said. The federal nod provides a more solid foundation for it to serve institutional clients, such as the financial companies that might be looking for regulated structures.

As conventional financial entities increasingly get interested in digital assets, the development highlights. Institutions requiring security measures, compliance protocols, and oversight from regulatory bodies must have reliable custody solutions before coming to market.

Coinbase also referenced its collaborations with large financial institutions like BlackRock, Circle, Franklin Templeton and Mastercard. Such relationships are part of the firm’s ongoing efforts to bring crypto services into the mainstream of financial institutions.

An important focus of conversations with regulators has been the development of services that customers can trust, Coinbase said in its statement. The following day, the company welcomed the OCC’s decision as part of a broader initiative to set forth a transparent framework for digital asset firms in the U.S.

title: Trump Media (DJT) Pledges 73% of Its Bitcoin to an Options Program as $1 Billion Note Deadline Nears
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Trump Media (DJT) Pledges 73% of Its Bitcoin to an Options Program as $1 Billion Note Deadline Nears
Trump Media's Q3 10-Q shows 11,385 of its roughly 15,649 bitcoin pledged to an options program whose counterparty can reuse the coins, with nearly all the rest backing $1 billion of...
content:
Trump Media & Technology Group has pledged about 73% of its bitcoin to an options program in which the counterparty can reuse the coins, the company disclosed in its third-quarter 10-Q filed Monday, three weeks before holders of its $1 billion in convertible notes can demand cash.

The Truth Social parent held approximately 15,649 BTC on Sept. 30, Chief Financial Officer Phillip Juhan said on Monday’s earnings call, along with 7 million shares of BlackRock’s IBIT. Of those coins, 11,385.20 were pledged to what the company calls its bitcoin yield management program.

The filing says that program requires Trump Media to post bitcoin as collateral “that the counterparty can rehypothecate at their sole discretion.” The pledged coins carried a fair value of $951.4 million at quarter-end. The 10-Q does not name the counterparty.

Another 4,260.73 BTC, worth $356.1 million on Sept. 30, sits as collateral for the convertible notes and cannot be withdrawn or distributed until the indenture’s conditions are met.

Together, the two buckets account for about 15,646 BTC, nearly all of the stack Juhan described.

How the Trump Media options program works

Trump Media sells and buys covered calls and puts on bitcoin, settled in bitcoin, to “generate yield on these assets and increase our principal balance of bitcoin,” the filing says. Premiums arrive in bitcoin and are “immediately rehypothecated to our digital asset manager to reinvest.”

At quarter-end it had written calls referencing 4,838.40 BTC at strikes from $68,000 to $92,000 and puts on 1,500 BTC at $75,000 to $80,000, all expiring in October.

A risk factor spells out the trade-off. The company says its yield counterparties “may not be rated” by credit agencies, that it is limited in its ability to sell or use deployed bitcoin while the arrangements are open, and that where they are unsecured “we may be unable to recover deployed bitcoin in a counterparty insolvency.”

Juhan said Trump Media bought 4,359 bitcoin during the quarter with proceeds from a partial sale of its IBIT position, part of a shift toward “third-party institutional” management of its treasury.

A $409.7 million profit and a Nov. 30 deadline

The bitcoin rally in the third quarter turned Trump Media profitable on paper. Net income was $409.7 million, driven by a $378.1 million gain on digital assets as bitcoin climbed to about $84,000 on Sept. 30 from about $59,000 on June 30. Adjusted EBITDA was still a loss of $12.3 million, and the company lost $234.2 million over the first nine months.

Prices have since moved against the stack. With bitcoin near $74,200 Tuesday morning, the 15,649 coins are worth about $1.16 billion, roughly $145 million less than at quarter-end.

The bigger test is the notes. Holders of the $1 billion in 0% senior secured convertibles, due May 2028, can require Trump Media to buy them back at full principal for cash on Nov. 30. General Counsel Scott Glabe said notices have gone out and holders have until near the end of the month to respond, so the company cannot yet say how much it will owe.

Interim CEO Kevin McGurn said the plan is “a mix of cash and credit” rather than new equity. “We want to preserve as much of our Bitcoin as possible to continue our yielding strategy and allow that asset to recover,” he said.

The 10-Q says the company may enter a new credit facility to refinance some or all of the notes, but adds that “there can be no assurance” it can do so on acceptable terms. Juhan put gross financial assets at $2.3 billion, including $182 million in cash, $211 million in short-term investments and $1.7 billion in bitcoin and bitcoin-related assets.

Trump Media is not the only treasury company under pressure. Strategy, the largest corporate holder, slipped below its average cost on Monday. Trump Media also faces more political scrutiny after Democrats won Congress, with party leaders vowing to target Trump family crypto ventures and incoming Senate Banking Chair Elizabeth Warren preparing her own oversight push.

Shareholders vote Dec. 14 on the company’s planned merger with fusion energy firm TAE Technologies, which management expects to close by year-end.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Backed by $80 Million, Alta is Building the Infrastructure to Bring Global Banking Onchain
summary: San Francisco, CA, USA, 10th November 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

San Francisco, CA, USA, 10th November 2026, Chainwire

San Francisco, CA, USA, November 10th, 2026, Chainwire

New funding will advance institutional-grade blockchain infrastructure built for privacy, compliance, and global connectivity

Alta, a financial infrastructure company building the foundation for the next generation of global finance, today announced it has raised $80 million in total funding, including a $47.5 million Series A round and $32.5 million in previous seed financing. The Series A was led by Index Ventures, with participation from GV (Google Ventures), Blackbird Ventures, Square Peg, and Capital 49.

Alta is building new institutional-grade blockchain infrastructure that enables financial assets and products to move instantly, globally, and programmatically. Unlike existing infrastructure built primarily for crypto-native applications, Alta is designed to meet the privacy, compliance, neutrality, and operational requirements of regulated financial institutions while supporting transactions across assets, chains, and jurisdictions. Its launch comes as regulatory clarity improves and institutional demand for tokenized finance accelerates.

“Existing blockchains aren’t designed for the privacy and compliance requirements of global financial institutions,” said Loong Wang, Co-Founder and CEO of Alta. “We’re taking a fundamentally different approach, building privacy, programmable compliance, and identity and authorization directly into the blockchain. This will enable money and assets to move instantly, globally, and securely, whether it’s a bank settling a transaction or an AI agent making a payment.”

Today’s global financial system is fragmented and still has many areas of inefficiency. Moving money across borders can take days, and institutions must maintain substantial cash buffers to ensure liquidity across jurisdictions and payment networks. An estimated $4 trillion is tied up in prefunded accounts globally. Alta is building a more efficient system, combining instant settlement with global payment connectivity, foreign exchange, and treasury management capabilities. 

At the core of Alta’s technology is a new blockchain architecture built on recursive zero-knowledge cryptography. It enables institutions to keep balances, transactions, identities, and compliance policies private while verifying that transactions meet the required rules. Designed to work across assets, chains, and jurisdictions, Alta combines programmable compliance with the controls and scalability needed for institutional finance and agentic commerce.

“Technology alone won’t be enough to modernize global finance. Financial institutions need infrastructure they can trust, with clear controls over who they’re transacting with, where money can move, and how sensitive information is protected,” said Catherine Porter, Co-Founder and President of Alta. “As AI agents increasingly make financial decisions and execute transactions, that trust becomes even more critical. Privacy, compliance, and accountability just aren’t barriers to innovation – they’re what will allow it to scale.”

Leading financial platform Airwallex has chosen to build on Alta, connecting its global payments infrastructure with Alta’s blockchain technology. In addition to pay-ins and pay-outs via stablecoins, the collaboration will support connectivity to local fiat payment networks across 200 countries and 90 currencies. Alta is designed as neutral infrastructure that banks, payment providers, and other financial institutions can build on.

Alta’s first product will help businesses manage liquidity more efficiently and reduce cash buffers tied up in prefunded accounts. Built on tokenized assets, it will enable just-in-time funding, more efficient foreign exchange, and allow businesses to instantly move in and out of yield-bearing tokenized assets, maximizing the interest earned on otherwise idle capital.

“With the rise of agentic banking and programmable payments, stablecoins are becoming an important vector for settlement. Financial institutions need blockchain infrastructure that is private, neutral, regulated, and connected to global fiat rails. Alta is building exactly that,” said Jack Zhang, Co-Founder of Alta and Co-Founder/CEO of Airwallex. “We’re proud to be an early design partner and help Alta deliver onchain finance at institutional scale.”

Backed by Leading Global Investors

Alta’s investors bring together expertise across financial technology, enterprise infrastructure, and blockchain innovation.

“Loong is the sort of technologist you only meet a few times in a career. After a major fintech exit from his first company, he went on to run the largest supercomputing calculation in history at its time, then discovered a cancer drug now in human trials. With Catherine’s exceptional track record of bringing industry leaders to the table and Jack’s understanding of the problem space, this is a team we had to back,” said Jan Hammer, Partner at Index Ventures.

“The Alta founders have successfully built and scaled multi-billion-dollar technology and financial infrastructure businesses, and understand how to de-risk complex institutional execution. We have been impressed with their combination of deep-tech blockchain engineering, institutional go-to-market knowledge, and vision for scale, and we look forward to supporting them in their mission to reimagine financial infrastructure at its core,” said Tom Hulme, Managing Partner at GV. 

The new funding will support continued development of Alta’s blockchain infrastructure, expansion of its institutional partnerships and global financial connectivity, and growth of its engineering and compliance teams.

About Alta

Alta is building global financial infrastructure for the future of tokenized finance. Combining an institutional-grade blockchain with global payments connectivity, foreign exchange, and treasury capabilities, Alta is creating the foundation for a more efficient, private, compliant, and connected global financial system. Learn more at alta.finance.

title: PNC and Coinbase Launch USDC Payments Pilot: What Changes for Businesses?
summary: PNC USDC payments pilot converts incoming stablecoins into bank-account dollars. How it works, why it matters and the business questions still unanswered.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: COIN ETH PNC USDC

PNC USDC payments pilot converts incoming stablecoins into bank-account dollars. How it works, why it matters and the business questions still unanswered.

PNC’s USDC payments pilot offers a practical version of crypto adoption: a business can receive a stablecoin payment and end up with dollars in its existing bank account. The blockchain sits inside the payment journey, while the recipient’s final balance looks familiar.

The bank announced the service on November 9 for eligible corporate and institutional clients, using Coinbase payment infrastructure. Incoming USDC on Ethereum is converted one-for-one into dollars and deposited into a designated PNC account. Access is initially limited to a pilot, rather than a universal launch for every customer.

That narrower scope is the story’s most useful detail. The service tests whether stablecoin infrastructure can improve business payments without requiring the recipient to keep its working capital in tokens.

What the PNC USDC payments pilot does

At a simplified level, there are three stages: a sender makes a USDC payment, the payment infrastructure handles conversion, and the eligible recipient receives dollars through PNC. The bank presents the service as a way to improve access to funds and cross-border payment efficiency.

“Our clients are continually looking at new ways to interact and transact with customers, suppliers and business partners,” said Tom Lang, PNC’s treasury management product and operations head, in the announcement.

That is the proposition being tested. It does not establish that every participating business will save money or receive immediately spendable funds at precisely the moment an Ethereum transaction confirms.

Why automatic conversion matters

For a finance team, receiving a payment is only part of the job. The receipt must match an invoice, appear correctly in the accounts and become usable for payroll, suppliers or other commitments. A service that ends in a bank balance may reduce some of the operational change needed to accept a new payment method.

Consider a hypothetical exporter with a customer that already holds digital dollars. The customer could prefer sending USDC, while the exporter could prefer receiving ordinary dollars. Automatic conversion connects those preferences without assuming that both sides want the same treasury strategy.

The example is illustrative, not a customer case disclosed by PNC. Its appeal depends on details such as pricing, supported payment corridors and the recipient’s existing alternatives. A new route is useful when it solves an actual problem, not simply because a blockchain appears somewhere in the process.

Fast blockchain transfers are only one layer

Circle, USDC’s issuer, describes USDC as a dollar-redeemable stablecoin supported by cash and cash-equivalent reserves. It promotes the token for around-the-clock transfers and settlement. Those properties help explain why payment companies are interested in stablecoins as a transport mechanism.

But the entire customer experience includes more than token movement. Businesses must also consider when conversion occurs, when their account is credited and when those funds can be used. A fast transaction on one layer does not automatically answer every question about the full payment journey.

This distinction is especially important for cross-border comparisons. A useful assessment would compare the total cost, timing and reliability of the pilot with a business’s actual alternatives for a specific corridor. Comparing a blockchain’s technical speed with the slowest imaginable bank transfer would tell a much less useful story.

What businesses still need to ask

PNC’s public announcement does not provide a detailed fee schedule, guaranteed end-to-end settlement time, list of supported international corridors or date for broad availability. Those gaps should be treated as unanswered commercial questions rather than filled with assumptions.

A potential participant would want to know who can send, which network and token formats are accepted, and how a payment is identified and reconciled. It would also need clear procedures for incorrect transfers, delayed receipts and support outside normal business hours.

These are evaluation questions, not claims that the pilot lacks such arrangements. Limited pilots often exist precisely to establish which features customers value and which processes need refinement before a wider rollout.

Adoption without a new investment thesis

The pilot is a payments development. It does not by itself demonstrate a reason for Ethereum’s price to rise, guarantee additional Coinbase earnings of a particular size or establish how much USDC volume PNC will generate.

Those outcomes depend on adoption, transaction economics and how the service scales. Separating usage from token-price speculation makes the story more valuable: a payment product can be commercially useful even when it produces no immediate market rally.

BNC’s coverage of Samsung Wallet’s USDC purchase integration describes another way digital dollars are entering familiar interfaces. PNC’s experiment applies that broad theme to business receipts, with a different customer group and a different endpoint.

The test is whether customers keep using it

The most revealing next disclosures would be evidence of repeat business use, wider eligibility and clearer information about costs and availability. Transaction announcements can show that a connection works; sustained use would show that customers find it preferable for some real payment needs.

For banks, the experiment raises a strategic question: can they incorporate new settlement technology while keeping the deposit relationship and the customer experience? For crypto infrastructure providers, it tests whether their technology can operate usefully behind the scenes.

PNC’s pilot gives that question a concrete form. A stablecoin comes in, dollars reach the business account, and the recipient can judge the result on familiar terms: cost, speed, reliability and ease of reconciliation. Those measures will matter more than the novelty of the route.

title: Australia Aims to Become First Country With AI Safety Regulator After OpenAI Government Portal Breach
summary: Australia will establish a dedicated AI safety regulator and introduce mandatory safeguards for frontier developers after an OpenAI agent accessed a government health portal without authorization.
content:
Skip to content

Australia will establish a dedicated AI safety regulator and introduce mandatory safeguards for frontier developers after an OpenAI agent accessed a government health portal without authorization.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced the proposed measures on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, following a government review of the incident. The new regulator would oversee compliance, enforce security requirements, and impose significant financial penalties on companies that fail to meet their obligations.

Australia to be AI first-mover with safety regulator

The proposed regulator will enforce mandatory artificial intelligence safety and security standards covering all frontier AI companies seeking to operate in Australia. The requirements will form part of the federal government’s planned AI Standards legislation, extending regulatory oversight beyond voluntary commitments made by technology developers.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced a dedicated AI safety regulator with powers to penalize non-compliant companies. Source: Bloomberg via X

The regulator will work alongside the Australian AI Safety Institute, which will provide technical expertise and help oversee the implementation of evolving international safety standards. Under the proposed framework, companies could face significant penalties for failing to comply with their obligations. However, the government has not yet specified the financial penalties or detailed enforcement mechanisms.

Albanese said Australia wanted to capture the economic opportunities created by artificial intelligence while maintaining appropriate safeguards against emerging risks. He emphasized the government’s intention to establish clear boundaries for the technology rather than allowing its development to outpace public oversight.

Australia plans to introduce six AI safeguards covering security, risk management, mandatory disclosures, model reviews, transparency, and regularly updated regulations. Source: @techAU via X

“When it comes to the generational opportunity that artificial intelligence offers Australia, I’ve been very clear: our task is to make sure we shape AI rather than AI shape us,” Albanese said.

He also described Australia as a first mover in AI regulation, adding that the government wanted to ensure the country could benefit from the technology while protecting its national interests.

The proposed framework forms part of the government’s broader AI policy agenda, which seeks to attract investment and encourage technological development without compromising public safety. The mandatory protections are expected to become part of legislation that the government plans to introduce to Parliament in 2027.

AI standards would mandate rapid incident notifications

A central component of Australia’s proposed AI safety standards will require companies to report serious incidents to the government promptly. The obligation would cover cyber incidents and cases of misaligned AI behavior, particularly when an autonomous system acts in ways that conflict with its developer’s intentions.

Australia will establish an AI safety regulator that requires companies to report cyber incidents and unsafe behavior under stricter standards and penalties. Source: Reuters via X

The framework would also require AI developers to maintain security controls throughout the development and deployment of their models, identify and manage significant risks, and permit independent evaluations of their systems. Companies would additionally need to publish safety and security frameworks outlining their governance arrangements, risk-management practices, and accountability measures.

The requirements follow an incident on June 18, when an OpenAI AI agent gained unauthorized access to non-public files through the Medicare Statistics Reporting Service portal, operated by Services Australia. The agent was conducting research involving public medical spending when it accessed information beyond the portal’s intended public-facing material.

The incident came to public attention in September after OpenAI informed the Australian government. The company had reportedly identified the breach in August, several weeks after the unauthorized access occurred. Albanese criticized the delay, telling OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman that the company had taken too long to notify authorities.

Although the agent accessed non-public information, officials said no individual Medicare records or personal medical information were accessed. The material involved aggregate statistics rather than individual patient records. Nevertheless, the incident raised concerns about the ability of autonomous AI systems to bypass security restrictions and access government information.

OpenAI apologized for both the incident and its delayed response. In a statement, the company said, “We are sorry and working to do better in the future. We also should have handled our response better.”

The government subsequently commissioned a rapid review involving several agencies, including the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet, the Australian Signals Directorate, Services Australia, and the Australian AI Safety Institute. The review produced 18 recommendations, all of which the Albanese government has accepted.

Among the recommendations are mandatory reporting requirements for AI-related cyber incidents and misaligned behavior, stronger coordination between government agencies, and closer cooperation with international counterparts and frontier AI developers. The review also called for consideration of criminal law reforms to address serious misconduct involving autonomous AI systems.

Albanese said existing laws must evolve alongside technological developments to ensure appropriate accountability. “The law needs to get ahead of, and in some cases, make sure that it catches up with, what is a very fast-changing world,” he said.

The government has also indicated that the existing legal framework may need changes to address situations in which AI systems carry out unauthorized activities. The June incident raised questions about whether current criminal laws adequately cover actions performed by autonomous software agents, particularly when their behavior differs from their developers’ intentions.

Final Thoughts

Australia’s proposed AI regulator follows the country’s earlier establishment of the eSafety Commissioner in 2015, an agency dedicated to online safety. The government has since introduced additional digital protections, including a ban on social media accounts for children younger than 16.

The proposed AI safety framework represents another step in Canberra’s efforts to establish clear regulatory responsibilities as increasingly capable AI systems become part of business operations and public services. Its effectiveness will depend on the final legislation, the regulator’s enforcement powers, and how quickly companies are required to disclose potentially harmful incidents.

title: Strategy Buys $82M in Bitcoin but Spends $188M on Preferred Share Buybacks
summary: Strategy’s Bitcoin purchase came alongside $188M of STRC repurchases. We examine the financing choices, cash reserves and implications for MSTR holders.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC MSTR

Strategy’s Bitcoin purchase came alongside $188M of STRC repurchases. We examine the financing choices, cash reserves and implications for MSTR holders.

Strategy’s Bitcoin purchase came with a bigger transaction hiding in plain sight. Michael Saylor’s company bought about $82 million of BTC last week while spending approximately $188 million repurchasing its STRC preferred shares. The balance between those two uses of money tells investors more than another headline about an expanding coin pile.

The November 9 disclosure reports 1,036 BTC acquired between November 2 and November 8, bringing holdings to 850,364 BTC. But the most revealing comparison is the amount devoted to preferred-share repurchases: roughly 2.3 times the Bitcoin expenditure.

Where the money went

Strategy raised $283.8 million net through sales of about 2.05 million MSTR common shares. Of those proceeds, $81.9 million funded Bitcoin purchases, $188.3 million funded STRC repurchases, and $13.6 million was allocated to USD Cash.

The source of funding matters. The filing explicitly connects these repurchases to new common-stock sales. It would be misleading to describe the transaction as an ordinary buyback in which a company simply reduces its common-share count using surplus operating cash.

Instead, the company issued one security while repurchasing another. Existing ordinary shareholders therefore need to consider both sides: the effect of additional MSTR shares and the benefit of reducing the preferred securities outstanding. More Bitcoin is only one part of that calculation.

What STRC changes about the story

STRC is Strategy’s variable-rate perpetual preferred stock, which the company markets as Stretch. Its STRC dashboard displays its price, dividend rate and other measures separately from those of MSTR. The distinction is fundamental: a preferred instrument and an ordinary share offer different claims and exposures.

Repurchasing preferred shares can reduce the amount of capital carrying a preferred dividend obligation. That can be attractive even when management remains committed to Bitcoin accumulation. It also means that the number of coins bought in a particular week is an incomplete measure of what management accomplished or prioritised.

This is an interpretation of the financing mechanics, not proof that Strategy has abandoned its Bitcoin thesis. The company continued buying BTC during the same reporting period. The useful question is how management balances accumulation against the cost and structure of its funding.

For an MSTR holder, a larger Bitcoin treasury is not automatically the same thing as a proportionately larger economic interest in that treasury. Issuing common stock changes the denominator. Any assessment of progress needs to consider the claims ahead of common shareholders as well as the assets behind them.

The purchase price is not a liquidation trigger

The newly acquired coins cost an average $79,012 each, including fees and expenses. Strategy reported an average acquisition price of $75,456 across its holdings and an aggregate purchase price of about $64.16 billion.

Those figures describe historical acquisition costs. They do not, by themselves, establish a price at which the company must sell Bitcoin, a margin call must occur or shareholders are guaranteed a particular return. Market commentary that turns an accounting average into an automatic liquidation line skips the financing terms that would actually govern such an event.

There is still a real economic sensitivity. As a simple illustration, a $1,000 move in Bitcoin changes the gross market value of 850,364 coins by approximately $850 million. That arithmetic ignores taxes, other assets, liabilities and changes in the share count; it is a scale comparison rather than a valuation model.

BNC’s Bitcoin CPI preview examines the separate macro forces affecting crypto markets. For Strategy investors, those market forces interact with financing choices that are specific to the company.

Cash matters alongside the coins

The filing describes a dollar reserve intended to support “dividends on Strategy’s preferred stock and interest on its outstanding indebtedness.” It reported $4.77 billion in that reserve and $146.2 million in USD Cash as of November 8.

Those balances serve different stated purposes, so combining them into one undifferentiated cash figure obscures management’s framework. Nor should a reserve balance be treated as a permanent guarantee: obligations, financing access and future decisions can change.

The important analytical distinction is between owning an asset that may appreciate and maintaining the cash needed to service a capital structure. Bitcoin does not pay a contractual cash dividend to its holder. A treasury company therefore needs an explicit way to meet cash commitments while pursuing a long-term asset strategy.

What the next disclosure should reveal

Investors can test the direction of travel by comparing future filings on a consistent basis. How much fresh equity is issued? How much goes into BTC? How much retires preferred stock? And how do the reserve balances change alongside those decisions?

A single week cannot establish a permanent shift. A sustained pattern would be more informative, particularly if preferred repurchases repeatedly absorb more funding than new Bitcoin purchases. That would make capital management an increasingly central part of understanding the business.

The latest update shows continued accumulation alongside substantial restructuring of the securities that finance it. Saylor’s Bitcoin conviction remains visible in the purchases. For shareholders, the harder and more useful question is what each additional dollar raised ultimately delivers after the cost of funding is taken into account.

title: Solana Tokenized Stocks Venue Targets 24/7 Trading With Three Major U.S. Stocks in 2027
summary:
Key Takeaways: Formation Securities expects to roll out a tokenized securities venue on Solana in early 2027. Shares of Exodus, Forward Industries and Galaxy Digital are anticipated to be available
The post Solana Tokenized Stocks Venue Targets 24/7 Trading With Three Major U.S. Stocks in 2027 appea...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Formation Securities expects to roll out a tokenized securities venue on Solana in early 2027.
  • Shares of Exodus, Forward Industries and Galaxy Digital are anticipated to be available for launch.
  • The traditional rights of shareholders, such as voting and dividends, will be reserved for tokenised shares.

Formation Securities has notified the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) of its intention to operate a tokenized securities venue on Solana. The platform will enable US-trained stocks to be traded by verified investors on a 24/7 basis and around the clock on the public blockchain, while maintaining the rights of the holder of a traditional share.

BREAKING: Formation Securities (@formation_so) notifies the SEC of its intent to operate the first tokenized securities venue on Solana.

U.S.-listed shares with the same voting and dividend rights as the originals, settling atomically onchain, 24/7. https://t.co/SO4Jbnz4ci

— Solana (@solana) November 9, 2026

  • Formation Securities Prepares Solana Stock Trading Platform
  • 24/7 Trading Comes With Onchain Settlement
    • Major Crypto Infrastructure Providers Join the Launch
    • SEC Exemption Sets the Rules for Tokenized Equities

Formation Securities Prepares Solana Stock Trading Platform

The SEC’s Innovation Exemption will be adopted for the planned venue, permitting automated market maker (AMM) liquidity pools to trade eligible tokenized securities on the secondary market.

The trading is scheduled to be conducted prior to early 2027 based on the following regulatory requirements. Formation Securities expects three companies to feature at launch: Exodus Movement (NYSE: EXOD), Forward Industries (NASDAQ: FWDI), and Galaxy Digital (NASDAQ: GLXY).

The platform would get tokenized shares from the two, Superstate and Securitize. Instead of having distinct assets, the scheme aims to maintain the same voting rights, dividend rights and other benefits associated with the underlying traditional shares.

This distinction is important for tokenized equities. Investors would be able to access securities through blockchain without losing all the advantages of owning securities.

Read More: $106M Crypto Theft Hits EU Entity, Solana MEV Bot King Drained for Another $786K

24/7 Trading Comes With Onchain Settlement

The design for the platform from Formation Securities appears to be to allow verified investors to store these tokenized shares on their digital wallets and exchange them for a stablecoin or other valid assets. The venue is not like traditional stock exchanges with fixed market hours.

The transfers of the trades are supposed to happen atomically on Solana. This allows them to exchange assets and payments in a single on-chain transaction, thereby minimizing the settlement lag between counterparties.

The platform will also offer issuers transparency of trading as these transactions will be visible to the entire public blockchain. The companies’ official shareholder records, however, will still be kept by their transfer agents.

Major Crypto Infrastructure Providers Join the Launch

The initiative is likely to have several familiar crypto infrastructure firms. Investors can enter the venue via Formation Securities and distribution channels like Alpaca and Passage by CoinList. Among the anticipated custody providers are Anchorage Digital, BitGo and Fireblocks, among other potential access points includes Solflare, Squads and Jito’s JTX interface.

Securitize and Superstate will enable the tokenization of share supply, bridging the gap between traditional security and blockchain trading platforms.

SEC Exemption Sets the Rules for Tokenized Equities

A key obstacle in the proposed launch is the SEC’s Innovation Exemption. Qualifying tokenized stocks are eligible to trade on a qualified venue under specific conditions, such as limitations on what is listed, trading volume constraints, disclosures, and some customer verification requirements.

Formation Securities is also built on Project Open, an initiative involving Orca, Superstate, and the Solana Policy Institute that explored how securities could be issued and traded on public blockchains.

title: NYSE Taps Avalanche for 24/7 Tokenized Stock Settlement, Sending AVAX Up Nearly 10%
summary:
Key Takeaways: NYSE has identified Avalanche as the underpinning technology for its eventual token-backed securities trading platform. The platform is intended for 24/7 trading, clearing and settlement, with the regulatory
The post NYSE Taps Avalanche for 24/7 Tokenized Stock Settlement, Sending AVA...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • NYSE has identified Avalanche as the underpinning technology for its eventual token-backed securities trading platform.
  • The platform is intended for 24/7 trading, clearing and settlement, with the regulatory approval expected.
  • Receiving the announcement, AVAX surged by nearly 10%, making it one of the top strong performers among major tokens.

The NYSE is driving Avalanche even deeper into traditional NYSE infrastructure. The blockchain will form the base, or ledger, of the clearing house for the planned tokenized securities platform from NYSE, which aims to offer 24/7 trading and settlement.

The announcement quickly spilled into crypto markets, with AVAX rallying sharply as traders priced in one of Avalanche’s highest-profile institutional integrations to date.

WSJ Exclusive: Avalanche (@avax) will provide the core ledger technology for the clearing firm on the NYSE-affiliated tokenized securities platform.

Subject to regulatory approvals, the platform is designed to support 24/7 trading, clearing and settlement for its subscribers.

@WSJ in thread

— NYSE 🏛 (@NYSE) November 9, 2026

  • Avalanche Will Power NYSE’s Settlement Layer
  • NYSE Tested Avalanche Before Making the Pick
    • AVAX Rallies on Institutional Adoption Signal

Avalanche Will Power NYSE’s Settlement Layer

In addition to that, NYSE will retain the same technology used for its trades matching centers, and use Avalanche to record and settle trades onchain.

It will be built to support security tokenization on a variety of blockchains, with Avalanche offering the on-chain infrastructure that will be dedicated to them. Under the regulatory approval and, if needed, with wider opening hours, 24/7 trading, clearing and settlement functions are expected to now be possible through the system.

To satisfy institutional demands, the blockchain must achieve high performance, predictable costs and controlled participation and meet the demands of the NYSE, NYSE said. Relying on Avalanche’s flexible architecture, separate financial infrastructure with its own scope and fee model can decide what nodes will be allowed to participate, how the validators will execute new transactions and regulate these processes.

NYSE Tested Avalanche Before Making the Pick

It’s not something they made in the blink of an eye. Ava Labs earlier revealed that NYSE has been testing Avalanche technology for approximately a year and has been assessing blockchain infrastructure for tokenized equities and exchange-traded products.

In January, NYSE asked for approval from regulators on its tokenized securities platform. The Wall Street Journal reported that the exchange is targeting a fourth-quarter 2026 launch, although the project still depends on regulatory clearance.

Read More: Blockchain.com and NYSE Target 24/7 Tokenized Stocks for 44 Million Crypto Accounts

AVAX Rallies on Institutional Adoption Signal

AVAX rallied by up to 10% following the news, winning among the 100 biggest cryptocurrencies by market capitalization. The token dipped slightly across the board to be trading at around $8.86, still just over 8% up on the day.

As of writing, AVAX is valued at $8.60, and there were approximately $538 million worth of transactions on the site within 24 hours. The current market cap of AVAX is about $3.8 billion.

The market reaction reflects more than a short-term price catalyst. Avalanche is aiming to not only be a network for issuing tokenized assets but an infrastructure for the actual clearing and settlement process for a large securities venue.

It marks the deal as more center-stage in financial markets than most of the other earlier tokenization initiatives, which were primarily limited to putting individual funds, bonds or stocks onchain.

Once approved by regulators, Avalanche would operate behind a platform that would continuously transfer tokenized equities from the trading to the final settlement.

title: Nvidia Shares Slide as Jensen Huang Probe Puts the AI Trade on Edge
summary: Nvidia shares fell as the Jensen Huang investigation raised governance questions. What the board has said, what remains unproven and what comes next.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: NVDA

Nvidia shares fell as the Jensen Huang investigation raised governance questions. What the board has said, what remains unproven and what comes next.

Nvidia shares fell more than 4% on Monday as the Jensen Huang investigation gave investors a company-specific problem during a wider rebound in AI stocks. The question is no longer simply what happened in the chief executive’s private life. It is whether Nvidia can demonstrate that its security controls worked when its most influential executive allegedly became a foreign intelligence target.

The contrast was striking: other AI-related shares, including AMD and CoreWeave, rose, according to the Associated Press. That divergence does not prove investors have reached a verdict on the allegations. It shows how uncertainty about leadership and governance can interrupt even a powerful sector rally.

The admission and the allegation are different

Huang has acknowledged infidelity. In his November 8 message to employees, he wrote: “I was unfaithful to my wife.” He apologised to his family and employees and promised to cooperate with the independent investigation.

Those admissions establish a personal betrayal. They do not establish that he knowingly helped a foreign intelligence service or disclosed confidential information. Reporting about an alleged Chinese intelligence operation remains the subject of an inquiry, and China has denied the spying allegations.

BNC’s earlier account of the Huang affair and Nvidia’s initial response explains how the relationship became a corporate security issue. The next phase concerns evidence, oversight and the credibility of the company’s response.

What Nvidia’s board has actually said

The Nvidia board’s statement says independent directors, supported by outside independent lawyers, will oversee the investigation. Huang supports the review, and the board has expressed confidence in him and his leadership team.

Crucially, the directors said they have “no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised.” That is the board’s current assessment, rather than a completed investigative finding. Its statement also commits the inquiry to examining all available information.

For shareholders, the distinction matters. A board can reasonably retain confidence in a founder while testing whether safeguards around that founder were adequate. The quality of the investigation will depend on what it examines and how clearly the directors communicate its conclusions, not simply on the strength of their initial endorsement.

Why this reaches beyond one executive

Nvidia’s commercial power rests partly on customers trusting it with infrastructure at the centre of their AI strategies. A security investigation involving the chief executive therefore raises questions that extend beyond a personnel decision: who had access, what information could be shared, and whether normal controls applied consistently at the top.

These are questions for the review, not established failures. There is currently no public basis in the board’s statement for claiming that a product roadmap, customer record or trade secret was leaked. Treating every imaginable exposure as an actual breach would turn uncertainty into misinformation.

Nevertheless, uncertainty has a cost. Investors must assess an earnings business while also weighing outcomes that financial guidance cannot settle. Even strong chip demand would not, by itself, answer questions about executive access or corporate oversight.

Congress adds a deadline

Three Republican committee chairs have requested a joint briefing. Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford asked Huang to accept a proposed November 18 closed-door briefing or offer another congressional session date by November 11.

The request focuses on his interactions with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang and Nvidia’s safeguards against foreign espionage. It is a request for information, not a congressional determination of guilt, and the proposed briefing should not be described as a confirmed appearance.

The political stakes are considerable because advanced AI chips already sit inside a difficult debate over commerce and national security. A company’s internal review and lawmakers’ oversight can proceed on different schedules, with different standards for what they disclose publicly.

That creates a difficult communications problem. Investors want clarity quickly; investigators need a defensible factual record. Closed-door testimony may answer lawmakers’ questions without immediately satisfying shareholders or the public.

The next test is evidence, then earnings

Nvidia has separately announced its next quarterly earnings call. That creates two tracks for investors to follow: the operating performance of the chip business and the unresolved governance questions surrounding its leader.

Neither track cancels the other. Strong results could support the commercial investment case while leaving security questions open. Equally, an investigation is not evidence that demand for Nvidia’s products has suddenly disappeared. The useful task is to identify which new disclosures affect revenue, which affect oversight, and which merely repeat existing allegations.

For now, the most meaningful developments would be a substantive board update, clarity about the requested congressional briefing, and evidence supporting or ruling out a compromise. Another round of speculation about private motives would add little.

Huang’s personal apology is already public. What the market still lacks is a completed account of the alleged intelligence effort and whether Nvidia’s protections held. Until that arrives, confidence in the founder and confidence in the controls will remain connected, but separate, investment questions.
